papers.abstract: Malnutrition, altered body composition, and sarcopenia are common among patients with colorectal cancer (CRC) and are associated with poor treatment tolerance and adverse clinical outcomes. PhA, derived from BIA, reflects cellular membrane integrity and body cell mass and has been increasingly investigated as a potential marker of nutritional status and prognosis in oncology. However, the clinical relevance of PhA in patients with CRC has not yet been systematically synthesized. This systematic review was conducted in accordance with the PRISMA 2020 guidelines. PubMed, Embase, Web of Science, and Scopus were searched for observational studies published between January 2000 and October 2025 that assessed PhA in adult patients with CRC. Data extraction and risk-of-bias assessment using the AXIS tool were performed independently by two reviewers. Due to substantial heterogeneity in study design, outcome definitions, and PhA cut-off values, a narrative synthesis was conducted. A total of 10 studies involving 1,439 patients were included. Lower PhA values were consistently associated with adverse clinical outcomes. Four studies reported significantly shorter overall or progression-free survival among patients with low PhA. Four studies demonstrated associations between low PhA and unfavorable short-term outcomes, including postoperative complications, prolonged hospital stay, cancer-related complications, and early chemotherapy-related toxicity. Several studies also reported positive associations between PhA and indicators of nutritional status, body composition, muscle mass, muscle strength, and hydration balance. One longitudinal study showed that postoperative increases in PhA were accompanied by improvements in body composition parameters and reduced early chemotherapy-related toxicity. Current evidence indicates that BIA-derived phase angle is associated with nutritional status, body composition, treatment tolerance, and survival outcomes in patients with colorectal cancer. However, heterogeneity in measurement protocols and cut-off values limits direct clinical application. Standardized assessment methods and prospective studies are needed to establish CRC-specific reference values and to determine whether interventions that improve PhA can translate into improved clinical outcomes.

papers.abstract: Medical imaging is crucial for glioma management. Combined with MRI, amino acid PET may improve glioma diagnosis, biopsy targeting, and tumor delineation compared to structural MRI alone. Magnetic resonance spectroscopic imaging (MRSI) complements both structural MRI and PET by detecting metabolites such as N-acetylaspartate (NAA), creatine (Cr), and choline (Cho), which are markers for brain health and tumor malignancy, but is challenged by low spatial resolution. This study evaluates whether upscaled MRSI enhanced by deep learning can improve diagnostic accuracy and serve as a complement or alternative to PET for glioma classification. Ten glioma patients (ages 24-80) were included. Presurgical [18F]-FACBC PET/MRI, including proton 2D MRSI, was acquired for all patients. Thirty-two image-guided biopsies were sampled during surgery from the patients and classified as glioma tissue or non-tumor tissue, and according to IDH1 status. For each biopsy location, tumor-to-background ratio (TBR) and standardized uptake value (SUV) from PET, and tCho/NAA and tCho/tCr ratios from MRSI were calculated. ROC analysis was used to assess the accuracy of [18F]-FACBC PET and upscaled MRSI, and the combinations of these in classifying glioma vs non-tumor tissue and IDH1 status. Among the individual biomarkers evaluated, the tCho/NAA ratio from the deep learning-based model demonstrated the highest apparent AUC for classifying glioma vs. non-tumor tissue (AUC = 0.87, 95% CI: 0.66-1.0), compared with tCho/tCr (AUC = 0.81, 95% CI: 0.54-1:00), SUV (AUC = 0.71, 95% CI: 0.49-0.90), and TBR (AUC = 0.68, 95% CI: 0.48-0.86). Combining TBR with tCho/NAA and/or tCho/tCr improved tissue classification compared to either modality alone, where TBR+tCho/NAA+tCho/tCr showed the best results (AUC = 0.91, 95% CI: 0.71-1.0). MRSI was a poor predictor for IDH1-status (tCho/NAA: AUC = 0.67, 95% CI: 0.44-0.88 and tCho/tCr: AUC = 0.38, 95% CI: 0.17-0.60), while PET was an excellent predictor (SUV: AUC = 0.83, 95% CI: 0.66-0.95 and TBR: AUC = 0.82, 95% CI: 0.65-0.94) and the combination of SUV, tCho/NAA, and tCho/tCr was a best predictor (AUC = 0.96, 95% CI: 0.88-1.0). Combining DL-upscaled MRSI with [18F]-FACBC PET appeared to enhance discrimination between glioma and non-tumor tissue, a finding that warrants validation in larger, prospective studies.

papers.abstract: Accumulating evidence indicates that oral microbiota dysbiosis and periodontal pathogens contribute to the initiation and progression of oral squamous cell carcinoma (OSCC). However, the molecular mechanisms underlying the interaction between Porphyromonas gingivalis and the tumor immune microenvironment remain incompletely understood. This study aimed to investigate the potential role of a TLR4-associated ERK/CD155/TIGIT signaling pathway in P. gingivalis-mediated immunosuppressive microenvironment formation during OSCC progression. Genes associated with P. gingivalis and TIGIT were obtained from GeneCards and The Cancer Genome Atlas (TCGA) databases. Candidate hub genes were identified through bioinformatic analyses. An SCC7 syngeneic orthotopic transplantation mouse model was established, and SCC7 cells were injected together with Porphyromonas gingivalis. Tumor growth was assessed by measuring tumor volume and weight. Expression levels of TLR4, ERK1/2, CD155, and TIGIT were evaluated by immunohistochemistry and quantitative real-time PCR (qRT-PCR). Flow cytometry was performed to analyze tumor-infiltrating immune-cell populations. The TLR4 inhibitor TAK-242 was used to investigate the involvement of TLR4-associated signaling. Bioinformatic analysis identified TLR4 as a biologically relevant candidate hub gene potentially linking P. gingivalis-associated signaling and TIGIT-related immune regulation. Exposure to P. gingivalis significantly promoted tumor growth and increased the expression of TLR4, ERK1/2, CD155, and TIGIT in tumor tissues. Flow cytometric analysis revealed immune microenvironment remodeling characterized by increased proportions of CD4+ T cells, TIGIT-positive Tregs, and IL-10-positive cells, accompanied by reduced CD8+ T-cell infiltration and decreased frequencies of Ki67+CD8+ and CD44+CD8+ T cells. Treatment with the TLR4 inhibitor TAK-242 partially reversed these tumor-promoting, immunological, and molecular changes. Our findings suggest that exposure to P. gingivalis may promote OSCC progression by contributing to immune microenvironment remodeling. Increased expression of TLR4, ERK1/2, CD155, and TIGIT, together with the effects of TLR4 inhibition, supports the potential involvement of a TLR4-associated ERK/CD155/TIGIT signaling pathway in this process. However, the precise molecular mechanisms require further validation using genetic and functional approaches.

papers.abstract: Oral squamous cell carcinoma (OSCC) is the most common malignant tumor in the head and neck region. In locally advanced patients, neoadjuvant chemotherapy centered on cisplatin and 5-fluorouracil often leads to primary/acquired resistance, with a 5-year survival rate of less than 50%. Tumor microenvironment (TME) immunosuppressive remodeling is the core cause of chemotherapy failure. Adipokines secreted by cancer-associated adipocytes (CAAs) are the key mediators that link metabolic disorders, immune polarization and chemotherapy resistance. The adipokines leptin, adiponectin, chemerin, resistin, and GDF15 signal through pathways such as JAK2/STAT3, PI3K/AKT, NF-κB, and PPARγ to bidirectionally regulate the polarization phenotypes of tumor-associated macrophages (TAMs), myeloid-derived suppressor cells (MDSCs), CD4+/CD8+ T cells, and NK cells. Pro-cancer adipokines induce M2-type TAMs, MDSCs expansion, Th2/Th17 polarization, and effector T cell exhaustion, constructing an immunosuppressive microenvironment, upregulating DNA damage repair, drug efflux, and anti-apoptotic genes, and reducing cisplatin/5-FU chemosensitivity. The tumor-suppressive adipokine adiponectin promotes M1 macrophage and CD8+ effector T cell infiltration, reverses immunosuppression, and sensitizes chemotherapy. This article systematically reviews the origin and classification of adipokines, the polarization patterns of immune cells in the OSCC microenvironment, the molecular pathways by which various adipokines regulate immune polarization, and the complete mechanism by which immune polarization mediates chemotherapy resistance. It summarizes the value of clinical markers and targeted reversal strategies, points out current research bottlenecks, and looks forward to the translational prospects of metabolism-immunotherapy combined with chemotherapy, aiming to provide new metabolism-immune targets for overcoming chemotherapy resistance in oral cancer.

papers.abstract: TROP2 is expressed in many epithelial tumors including breast and lung cancers. It is a clinically validated ADC target based on approvals of sacituzumab govitecan for triple-negative breast cancer and datopotamab deruxtecan for HR-positive, HER2-negative breast cancer. An alternative cytotoxic approach was previously tested with PF-06664178/RN927C, an anti-TROP2 ADC with an auristatin payload, which entered clinical studies but could not be dosed efficaciously due to dose-limiting toxicities including skin rash, mucosal inflammation, and neutropenia. TroptimAb-SL-MMAE was engineered using an optimized anti-TROP2 sacituzumab antibody sequence (TroptimAb) to address issues related to hydrophobicity, non-specific uptake, and ADC developability. Sacituzumab was re-humanized and modified to enhance FcRn-mediated salvage which extended systemic half-life and potentially improving tumor distribution. Its affinity was avidity-tuned to preferentially bind cells with higher TROP2 expression to reduce on-target/off-tumor toxicity. An engineered cysteine in the Fc domain enabled generation of a homogeneous DAR2 ADC and shielded the linker-payload to reduce hydrophobicity and improve biophysical properties. Linker conjugation chemistry was also optimized to improve stability versus earlier cysteine-conjugated ADCs. We describe the preclinical profile of TroptimAb-SL-MMAE including its design, mechanism of action, anti-tumor activity, and pharmacokinetics.

papers.abstract: Metastatic castration-resistant prostate cancer (mCRPC) remains a lethal stage of prostate cancer with poor prognosis. Clinical trials for mCRPC are growing rapidly worldwide. However, a comprehensive systematic analysis of the global research and development landscape in mCRPC remains lacking. This study queried the Trialtrove database for interventional trials in mCRPC registered between January 1, 2020 and March 27, 2026. After exclusion of unrelated trials and non-therapeutic studies, 474 trials were analyzed. The therapeutic landscape for mCRPC has evolved into a highly diversified and dynamic field, overwhelmingly dominated by early-phase investigations. Targeted therapy, particularly PARP inhibitors, remain the leading class, while radiopharmaceutical therapy (RPT), centered on 177Lu-PSMA, has reached a mature stage of development. Immunotherapy is expanding beyond checkpoint blockade into bispecific T-cell engagers and cellular therapies, and endocrine therapy is being reshaped by PROTAC degraders. Antibody-drug conjugates (ADCs) are also gaining momentum, with B7 homolog 3 protein (B7-H3) as the most actively pursued targets. Combination regimens account for 39.2% of trials. mCRPC clinical research landscape has diversified remarkably, shifting from conventional chemotherapy and endocrine therapy toward mechanism-based, biomarker-guided, and combination-oriented strategies.

papers.abstract: Lung adenocarcinoma (LUAD) is the most common histological subtype of lung cancer, with a dismal prognosis partly attributed to immune evasion mediated by T cell dysfunction within the tumor microenvironment. However, the molecular determinants governing CD8+ cytotoxic T lymphocyte functional competence remain incompletely understood. Chloride intracellular channel 3 (CLIC3) has been implicated in cancer progression, but its role in T cell immunity within the LUAD TME is unknown. We performed single-cell RNA sequencing on tumor tissues from nine LUAD patients spanning three pathological stages (adenocarcinoma in situ [AIS], minimally invasive adenocarcinoma [MIA], and invasive adenocarcinoma [IAC]), integrated with spatial transcriptomics, TCGA-LUAD bulk RNA-seq analysis, and flow cytometric validation in an independent cohort of 32 LUAD patients. Functional module scoring and pseudotime trajectory analysis were applied to characterize CLIC3-associated CTL functional states. CLIC3 was predominantly expressed in CTLs and showed a stage-associated decline from AIS to MIA to IAC. CLIC3+ CTLs exhibited significantly higher module scores for cytotoxicity, cytoskeleton remodeling, interferon signaling, and chemotaxis compared to CLIC3- CTLs. Pseudotime trajectory analysis indicated that CLIC3+ cells were positioned at one end of the inferred transcriptional continuum, corresponding to a functionally active state, while CLIC3- cells were positioned at the other, corresponding to a dysfunctional state, accompanied by a decline in CD247, GZMB, PRF1, and TNF along the trajectory. High CLIC3 expression in TCGA-LUAD was associated with significantly longer overall survival. Flow cytometry showed a stage-associated decrease in CLIC3 expression on CD8+ T cells with increasing tumor invasiveness and poor differentiation. CLIC3 serves as a novel marker of CTL functional competence in LUAD, and its stage-associated downregulation reflects T cell dysfunction during tumor progression. CLIC3 expression in CD8+ T cells may represent a predictive biomarker for immunotherapeutic response and a potential target for restoring T cell function in LUAD.

papers.abstract: Current clinical diagnostic models lack sufficient sensitivity and specificity for Hepatoblastoma (HB) individualized prediction. This study aimed to identify robust hub genes for HB diagnosis and molecular subtyping by integrating multiple transcriptomic datasets and machine learning algorithms. Four merged GEO hepatoblastoma datasets (GSE131329, GSE132037, GSE104766, GSE133039) were analyzed by differential expression and WGCNA to identify HB-related genes. Further use three algorithms (LASSO, SVM-RFE, Random Forest) to identify central genes. In addition, consensus clustering was used for molecular typing, and four deconvolution algorithms (TIMER, MCPcounter, xCell, quanTIseq) were used to characterize the tumor microenvironment. The biological function of SDS in hepatoblastoma was elucidated through in vitro experiments (CCK-8 detection, colony formation assay, Transwell assay), as well as in vivo using a xenograft mouse model. A total of 268 differentially expressed genes (77 up, 191 down) were identified. WGCNA revealed the blue module as most correlated with HB (correlation coefficient 0.66). Three machine learning algorithms jointly selected four hub genes (CLEC1B, ITGA6, SDS, TTC36). Consensus clustering based on these four genes stratified HB into two subtypes (Clust1, Clust2). Clust1 exhibited enhanced immune infiltration and activation of complement, IFN-α, and IL6-JAK-STAT3 pathways. Low SDS expression associated with cell cycle pathways, whereas high SDS expression associated with immune-related pathways. Functionally, SDS overexpression significantly suppressed HB cell proliferation, migration, invasion, and colony formation, while promoting apoptosis in vitro, and markedly reduced tumor growth in vivo. Integrated machine learning identified CLEC1B, ITGA6, SDS, and TTC36 as robust diagnostic genes for hepatoblastoma. SDS, in particular, exerts a tumor-suppressive role and is closely linked to the immune microenvironment, making it a promising diagnostic biomarker and therapeutic target in HB.

papers.abstract: High-grade gliomas remain among the most aggressive tumors in neuro-oncology. Although prognosis is strongly influenced by tumor biology, survival in low- and middle-income countries is also shaped by health-system factors, including delayed diagnosis, limited surgical infrastructure, incomplete adjuvant therapy, and restricted molecular diagnostics. The implementation of the 2021 World Health Organization Classification of Central Nervous System Tumors has further exposed diagnostic inequities, as integrated histomolecular classification depends on molecular tools that are not uniformly available in resource-limited settings. This systematic review and meta-analysis aimed to synthesize contemporary evidence on survival outcomes, surgical access, extent of resection, adjuvant treatment delivery, and molecular diagnostic gaps among patients with high-grade gliomas treated in low- and middle-income countries. A systematic search was conducted following PRISMA 2020 recommendations. MEDLINE/PubMed, Embase, Scopus, Web of Science, Cochrane CENTRAL, Global Index Medicus, LILACS, African Index Medicus, IndMED, and Google Scholar were searched for studies published between January 2016 and May 2026. Eligible studies included patients with histologically or molecularly confirmed WHO grade 3 or grade 4 gliomas treated in low- or middle-income countries and reporting survival, surgical-access, adjuvant-treatment, or molecular-diagnostic outcomes. The protocol was registered in PROSPERO as CRD420261398058. A total of 30 independent studies met the predefined eligibility criteria and were included in the qualitative synthesis. Twenty-four studies contributed overall survival data, 18 reported surgical-access outcomes, 21 evaluated adjuvant-treatment delivery, and 12 examined molecular-diagnostic availability. Most included investigations were retrospective institutional cohorts, although registry-based studies, randomized clinical trials, and molecular implementation studies were also identified. Survival outcomes varied substantially across healthcare settings and were consistently influenced by delayed diagnosis, limited access to maximal safe resection, incomplete radiotherapy, restricted temozolomide availability, treatment abandonment, and insufficient molecular characterization. Survival in high-grade gliomas in low- and middle-income countries is not determined by tumor biology alone. It is shaped by sequential "survival gates": timely diagnosis, access to maximal safe resection, completion of radiotherapy and temozolomide-based chemotherapy, molecular classification, and longitudinal follow-up. Future strategies should move beyond simple guideline translation and focus on scalable neuro-oncology pathways that improve surgical capacity, adjuvant-treatment continuity, and access to essential molecular diagnostics. https://www.crd.york.ac.uk/PROSPERO/view/CRD420261398058, identifier CRD420261398058.

papers.abstract: Mushroom-derived polysaccharides are widely promoted as anticancer immune modulators, but interpretation is weakened by imprecise product identity, chemically non-equivalent preparations, and extrapolation across evidence levels. This critical narrative review evaluates beta-glucans, heteropolysaccharides, polysaccharide-protein complexes, crude fractions, modified derivatives, and multicomponent extracts as preparation-specific adjunct candidates. Receptor-level evidence is strongest for general fungal beta-glucan systems, particularly Dectin-1/Syk/CARD9 signaling and conditional complement receptor 3 cooperation; direct transfer of those mechanisms to individual mushroom preparations requires product-specific causal testing. Selected animal studies support myeloid remodeling, dendritic-cell and natural-killer-cell effects, and T-cell activation, but route, exposure, product characterization, and model limitations constrain translation. Human evidence remains heterogeneous: historical randomized PSK studies reported benefit in specific adjuvant chemotherapy settings, a later phase III lentinan trial was negative for overall survival, and small maitake, Agaricus, and pleuran studies mainly report immune surrogates. Direct clinical evidence with checkpoint inhibitors, therapeutic antibodies, or cancer vaccines is not established. The field should therefore move from species-level claims to product-level development with authenticated source material, orthogonal structural analysis, contaminant control, mechanism-linked potency, route-specific pharmacokinetics, tumor pharmacodynamics, and randomized testing against contemporary standard care. Mushroom-derived polysaccharide immunomodulators remain plausible research candidates, but neither the class nor unstandardized mushroom foods or supplements are clinically validated substitutes for established cancer treatment.

papers.abstract: Acquired resistance to sorafenib in hepatocellular carcinoma (HCC) is accompanied by coordinated changes in oxidative-stress handling and regulated cell-death pathways, yet how membrane organisation connects these adaptations is not fully resolved. We therefore examined whether B4GALNT1, a ganglioside biosynthetic glycosyltransferase, couples changes in ganglioside composition and lipid-raft architecture to ferroptosis regulation and caspase-1/GSDMD-associated signalling in sorafenib-resistant HCC. We combined TCGA-LIHC analysis, single-cell transcriptomics, pathway-level analyses, and graph attention network modelling with a treatment-annotated local cohort of 92 patients with HCC who received sorafenib. Functional experiments were conducted in Huh7/Huh7-SR cells and additional liver-tumour models using B4GALNT1 gain- and loss-of-function, an independent second-sgRNA knockout clone, GM1 rescue, and re-expression of either wild-type B4GALNT1 or the catalytic-loss D358A variant. Validation included ganglioside profiling, detergent-resistant membrane isolation, lipid-raft disruption/repletion, ferroptosis-directed pharmacology, cell-death measurements, and xenograft studies. B4GALNT1 was enriched in tumour-associated hepatocyte populations and was upregulated in Huh7-SR cells. In the local cohort, higher B4GALNT1 protein abundance tracked with less favourable response to sorafenib and poorer survival outcomes. Increasing B4GALNT1 shifted ganglioside abundance toward GM2/GM1/GD2 and increased GM1-enriched raft-associated fractions, whereas knockout produced reciprocal changes. B4GALNT1-high cells showed increased GPX4 and SLC7A11, reduced lipid peroxidation and labile Fe2 +, and lower ferroptotic injury. At the same time, caspase-1/GSDMD-associated signalling and IL-1β/IL-18 release increased without widespread terminal membrane lysis. Exogenous GM1 partially rescued knockout-associated changes, and wild-type B4GALNT1 restored the phenotype more effectively than the D358A mutant. Concordant directional effects were observed in additional cell models and in xenografts. The data are consistent with a model in which B4GALNT1 reshapes ganglioside composition and GM1-enriched membrane microdomains, thereby supporting a drug-adapted state that combines greater ferroptosis resistance with restricted caspase-1/GSDMD-associated membrane permeabilisation. This integrated phenotype accompanies reduced sorafenib responsiveness and offers a mechanistic basis for acquired resistance in HCC. B4GALNT1 is associated with sorafenib resistance and poorer outcomes in treated HCC. B4GALNT1 remodels gangliosides and lipid rafts, limiting ferroptotic injury. Caspase-1/GSDMD signalling increases without widespread terminal membrane lysis. Genetic rescue and cross-model studies support B4GALNT1 specificity.

papers.abstract: Transcription factors (TFs) are often considered undruggable due to their structural complexity. mRNA technologies can overcome this therapeutic limitation by enabling dynamic protein replacement therapies. Here, we explore the TF activity of LCOR (Ligand-dependent corepressor), which suppresses tumor growth, at least in part by inducing the antigen presentation machinery (APM) in tumor cells and constraining cellular plasticity. These effects facilitate tumor immune recognition and immune-mediated tumor eradication. We used poly β-(amino esters) (pBAE) nanoparticles (NPs) for local delivery of Lcor mRNA in multiple breast cancer models. pBAE-NPs efficiently encapsulate mRNA and facilitate cellular uptake, achieving optimal endosomal escape, resulting in high transfection efficiency in vitro and in vivo, restoring LCOR function in tumor cells and engaging their APM. In preclinical models, intratumoral delivery of Lcor mRNA reduced tumor growth. Importantly, the combination of Lcor mRNA-loaded RH-pBAE-NPs with anti-PDL1 or anti-CTLA4 immunotherapies eradicated most of the tumors in our preclinical TNBC model. Overall, our nanotherapeutic strategy emerges as an innovative TF-replacement therapy in a lock-in/wipe-out fashion, leveraging the immunogenic effects of LCOR to eradicate breast cancer tumors when combined with immunotherapy.

papers.abstract: Electroencephalography (EEG) monitoring during pediatric anesthesia may improve perioperative safety by optimizing anesthetic titration and reducing adverse outcomes. However, little is known about patient and caregiver perceptions regarding this technology and its implementation into routine anesthesia care. This study evaluates perceived importance, utility, and extent of reassurance provided by intra-operative EEG monitoring among pediatric patients and their parents. Secondary aims include identifying concerns surrounding general anesthesia (GA), concerns surrounding EEG monitoring, cost and willingness to pay, and sociodemographic and medical factors shaping these attitudes. We conducted an exploratory cross-sectional survey at a tertiary pediatric hospital in Singapore between July 2022 and September 2025. Respondents were parents of children aged 1-18 years and children aged 12-18 scheduled for elective procedures under general anesthesia. A 16-item anonymized questionnaire assessed perceptions of intra-operative EEG monitoring, concerns about anesthesia, and attitudes regarding the cost of EEG monitoring. Of 400 respondents (100 children, 300 parents), 83.5% rated intra-operative brain monitoring as "very" or "quite" important and 93% reported feeling more reassured by its use. Children were most concerned about intraoperative awareness and failure to awaken, whereas parents were most concerned about anesthetic side effects and dosage. Parents with higher education and whose children had prior anesthetic exposure reported greater reassurance from EEG monitoring. Cost was the leading concern regarding EEG monitoring, particularly among parents from families residing in public housing. Despite this, most parents (75%) and children (59%) expressed willingness to pay for EEG monitoring. Pediatric patients and parents viewed intra-operative EEG monitoring as important and reassuring, and expressed willingness to support its implementation despite cost concerns. These findings suggest that families are unlikely to be a major barrier to EEG adoption and highlight the need for clinician- and system-level strategies to integrate EEG monitoring into family-centered pediatric anesthesia care.

papers.abstract: Anemia represents a frequent and clinically burdensome complication in patients with primary lung cancer receiving platinum-based regimens, yet robust risk stratification tools that integrate multidimensional clinical data and undergo external validation remain scarce. This multicenter study sought to develop and externally validate a machine learning-based predictive model for CIA in this population. A total of 3,434 patients with primary lung cancer were retrospectively enrolled from two geographically distinct institutions, with 3,097 assigned to the training/internal validation set (7:3 split) and 337 retained as an independent external validation set. Variables with missing rates exceeding 30% were excluded, and remaining missing data were imputed using multiple imputation by chained equations (MICE). Thirteen candidate predictors were preselected via univariate screening and least absolute shrinkage and selection operator (LASSO) regression. Nine machine learning algorithms were developed and comparatively evaluated using area under the receiver operating characteristic curve (AUC), calibration plots, and decision curve analysis. Model interpretability was achieved through SHapley Additive exPlanations (SHAP). The primary outcome was defined as hemoglobin levels < 100 g/L (CTCAE Grade ≥ 2) recorded during the first two cycles of chemotherapy. Among the nine candidate models, LightGBM achieved the highest discriminative performance, with AUCs of 0.871 (95% CI: 0.852-0.891) in the training set, 0.797 (95% CI: 0.763-0.831) in internal validation, and 0.684 (95% CI: 0.626-0.742) in the external validation set derived from Linfen Central Hospital. Calibration and decision curve analyses consistently demonstrated superior agreement and net clinical benefit for LightGBM across all three datasets. SHAP-based interpretation identified lymphocyte count, D-dimer, alanine aminotransferase, total bilirubin, sex, and albumin as the six most influential predictors, with D-dimer, female sex, and outpatient admission positively associated with anemia risk, whereas lymphocyte count, liver function indices, and albumin showed inverse associations. The LightGBM-based model developed herein demonstrates acceptable and moderate predictive performance, satisfactory calibration, and potential clinical utility across geographically diverse populations, offering a preliminary risk-stratification tool for early identification of lung cancer patients at elevated anemia risk prior to chemotherapy initiation. However, given the modest external validation performance, cautious interpretation and further refinement are warranted before widespread clinical deployment.

papers.abstract: To compare the therapeutic outcomes of neoadjuvant chemotherapy followed by interval debulking surgery (NACT-IDS) and primary debulking surgery (PDS) in patients with advanced epithelial ovarian cancer (AEOC) and to evaluate factors associated with prognosis. This retrospective study included 97 patients with AEOC treated between April 2015 and July 2020. According to treatment strategy, 36 patients underwent PDS and 61 underwent NACT-IDS. Overall survival (OS), progression-free survival (PFS), and perioperative outcomes were compared between the two groups. Kaplan-Meier analysis and Cox proportional hazards regression were used to evaluate survival outcomes. Additional adjusted models were used to account for baseline imbalance. Because CA-125 normalization occurred after treatment initiation, it was defined as a serum CA-125 concentration of ≤35 U/mL and analyzed as a time-dependent covariate. Significant baseline differences were observed between the groups in age, BMI, baseline CA-125 level, and FIGO stage (all P<0.05). During a median follow-up of 43 months [95% CI (39.87, 50.32)], 53 of 97 patients (54.64%) died. Median OS was 41 months in the PDS group and 43 months in the NACT-IDS group, and median PFS was 20 months in both groups. No significant differences were found in unadjusted OS or PFS between the groups (OS: log-rank P = 0.484; PFS: log-rank P = 0.410). After adjustment for age, BMI, log-transformed baseline CA-125 level, and FIGO stage, treatment strategy was not associated with OS [adjusted HR = 0.88, 95% CI (0.49, 1.58), P = 0.667] or PFS [adjusted HR = 1.07, 95% CI (0.64, 1.79), P = 0.798]. Patients who achieved complete cytoreduction (R0) had longer median OS than those with incomplete cytoreduction (R1+R2) [43 vs. 38 months, P = 0.025] and longer median PFS [22 vs. 18 months, P = 0.040]. After adjustment, NACT-IDS remained associated with shorter operation time, lower intraoperative blood loss, earlier initiation of postoperative chemotherapy, and a lower likelihood of drainage-tube placement, whereas its association with postoperative complications was no longer statistically significant. Residual disease was associated with higher mortality [adjusted HR = 2.61, 95% CI 1.10-6.18, P = 0.029]. CA-125 normalization was associated with lower hazards of death [time-dependent adjusted HR = 0.59, 95% CI 0.35-0.99, P = 0.047] and progression or death [time-dependent adjusted HR = 0.63, 95% CI 0.42-0.95, P = 0.026]. In this exploratory single-center retrospective non-randomized cohort, NACT-IDS was associated with shorter operation time, lower intraoperative blood loss, earlier initiation of postoperative chemotherapy, and less frequent drainage-tube placement than PDS, but not with a significantly lower adjusted postoperative complication rate or with OS or PFS. These findings should not be interpreted as evidence of equivalent survival efficacy or causal treatment benefit. Residual disease was associated with poorer survival, whereas documented CA-125 normalization showed a favorable time-dependent prognostic association.

papers.abstract: The tumour microenvironment comprises a variety of cell types that interact with malignant cells, influencing both cancer progression and the patient response to therapy. Given the intricate interactions among these components, assessing how signalling pathways contribute to cancer progression by acting on different components of the TME is particularly complex. Multiplexed imaging allows simultaneous assessment of signalling in multiple of these components. Here, we utilise a highly multiplexed dataset of 61 markers across 746 colorectal tumours to investigate how complex mTOR signalling in different tissue compartments influences patient prognosis. We found that mTOR pathway signalling in immune cells correlates with favourable patient survival. Advanced spatially-aware analysis of signalling activities using graph neural networks revealed that the positive association between immune mTOR signalling and patient survival was more pronounced in tumours with features of a more differentiated morphology. Integrative analysis using TCGA data and spatial transcriptomics confirmed a role for immune mTOR signalling in immune activation, accompanied by reduced TGF-β signalling. Our work highlights the importance of adopting a personalised approach to targeting mTOR in cancer patients and establishes a framework for studying cell type-specific signalling in the TME.

papers.abstract: Germline and somatic mutations in POT1 promote oncogenesis by enabling aberrant telomere elongation. For inherited POT1 mutations, it remains unclear whether elongated telomeres are transmitted to the next generation and whether the inherited long telomeres elevate cancer risk. Using a nanopore sequencing approach that provides haplotype-specific telomere length resolution, we examined telomere inheritance in families carrying POT1 mutations. We found that offspring preferentially inherit their longest telomeres from the carrier parent, consistent with extensive germline telomere elongation, whereas comparatively short telomeres predominantly derive from the non-carrier parent. Analysis of carrier and non-carrier siblings demonstrated that telomeres from both parents are elongated in POT1 carriers, with preferential elongation of the shortest telomeres. These findings support a potential mechanism of genetic anticipation in which POT1 mutations progressively deplete short telomeres capable of enforcing telomere-based tumor suppression from the carrier germline. Therefore, telomeres inherited from both parents jointly shape telomere-based tumor suppressive barriers.

papers.abstract: SETD2 is a critical tumor suppressor in lung cancer that catalyzes histone H3 lysine 36 (H3K36) trimethylation. Oncogenic histone H3 alleles, including H3K36M, causally drive cancer formation by dominantly inhibiting SETD2 and other H3K36 methyltransferases. Here we show that expression of the H3K36M oncogene paradoxically suppresses tumor growth in KRAS-driven lung cancer by promoting transcription of repetitive elements and accumulation of cytoplasmic dsRNA, activating antiviral-like immune clearance. Unexpectedly, all attendant effects of H3K36M expression require SETD2 activity despite widespread loss of H3K36 trimethylation. Reducing H3K36 dimethylation through genetic or pharmacologic attenuation of NSD2 phenocopies H3K36M expression, revealing NSD2 as the relevant target through which H3K36M triggers immune activation. Mechanistically, H3K36M expression or NSD2 attenuation reveals a SETD2-dependent mechanism that limits EZH2-mediated repression of repetitive elements, enabling dsRNA accumulation and immune activation. These findings establish opposing roles for NSD2- and SETD2-dependent H3K36 methylation in lung tumor immunity and reveal an NSD2-SETD2-EZH2 axis that can be targeted to modulate viral mimicry and immune surveillance in cancer.

papers.abstract: Pulmonary tuberculosis (TB), caused by lung infection with Mycobacterium tuberculosis (Mtb), often manifests both alveolar pneumonia and aggregation of immune cells containing Mtb, termed granulomas, within the same lung. Here, we integrate spatial transcriptomics, single-cell RNA sequencing, high-resolution imaging, and functional assays of lung biopsies from four men with pulmonary TB to compare alveolar pneumonia with adjacent granulomas. We find that alveolar TB pneumonia is enriched for TREM2⁺ lipid-laden macrophages characterized by increased lipid metabolism gene expression, reduced T cell infiltration, attenuated antimicrobial gene expression, and abundant Mtb transcripts and antigens. By contrast, neighboring granulomas exhibit organized lymphoid architecture and robust antimicrobial programs. In vitro, Mtb lipids induce TREM2 expression, activate TREM2-DAP12 signaling, and promote lipid droplet accumulation in primary human monocyte-derived macrophages (MDM). Furthermore, TREM2+ MDMs are more susceptible to in vitro Mtb infection. When treating MDMs with 1,25-dihydroxyvitamin D₃, which induces antimicrobial macrophage programs, TREM2+ MDM numbers, lipid droplet abundance and Mtb viability are decreased. Thus, we propose a spatially localized, alveolar pneumonia-intrinsic TREM2⁺ macrophage program that potentially contributes to Mtb persistence in pulmonary TB infection in humans.

papers.abstract: Coupled cluster theory using a Kohn-Sham density functional reference can dramatically outperform the standard Hartree-Fock-based approach for strongly correlated systems, but the origin of these improvements has remained unclear. We show these improvements arise from differences in the one-particle density as encoded into the Fock matrix, not from the nature of the orbitals themselves, as is commonly assumed. Exploiting this insight, Kohn-Sham references enable near-chemical accuracy for electronic and thermochemical properties of transition metal dimers and main group compounds. Notably, Kohn-Sham coupled cluster qualitatively recovers the entire chromium dimer potential energy surface, a notorious failure case for conventional methods. We further introduce a density difference diagnostic that detects multireference character and guides the selection of optimal references at mean-field cost. Together, these results establish a practical route to treating strong correlation within quantum chemistry's "gold standard" framework, with immediate implications for machine learning potential development and materials research, which rely heavily on density functional theory.

papers.abstract: Hypertension has paradoxical prothrombotic-hemorrhagic predisposition toward cerebral infarction and intracerebral hemorrhage (ICH), but the mechanism remains poorly understood. We observed Angiotensin II (Ang II) inhibited coagulation by activating antithrombin through heparin-like acceleration of antithrombin-thrombin interaction. Ang II allosterically modulates the 386-397 loop of antithrombin to enhance thrombin inhibition. In vivo, single injection of Ang II inhibited coagulation, alleviating thrombosis and aggravating ICH. Conversely, anti-Ang II monoclonal antibody promoted coagulation, aggravating thrombus formation and alleviating ICH. Notably, the blockage or deficiency of Ang II receptor had no significant effect on the alleviated thrombus formation or aggravated hemorrhage elicited by Ang II, suggesting the phenotypes were independent of Ang II receptor. In hypertensive mice, anti-Ang II monoclonal antibody significantly promoted coagulation and ameliorated ICH. These results identify Ang II as a key coagulation regulator with heparin-like function, suggesting that targeting Ang II-coagulation pathway could be a novel strategy to mitigate cerebral bleeding.

papers.abstract: The Novel Organic Cation Transporter 1 (OCTN1) facilitates the uptake of endogenous metabolites and therapeutic drugs across diverse tissues. Recognized as a key transporter for the antioxidant ergothioneine (ET), OCTN1 also mediates the cellular entry and release of various cationic compounds. Dysregulation of OCTN1 has been implicated in cancer progression and drug interaction. In non-neuronal systems, OCTN1-mediated acetylcholine (ACh) transport has been implicated in promoting cancer progression by enhancing tumor cell proliferation and invasion. Despite its physiological and clinical relevance, the structural mechanisms underlying substrate recognition and transport by OCTN1 have remained poorly understood. Here, we present cryo-EM structures of human OCTN1 in both apo and ET-bound states, revealing the binding site of ET and elucidating conformational changes essential for sodium-dependent substrate transport. Furthermore, structure-based virtual screening identified mebendazole (MBZ) as a potent inhibitor targeting OCTN1, effectively suppressing the proliferation of cervical and lung cancer cells. Our findings provide a structural framework for understanding OCTN1 function and inform strategies to target this transporter in cancer.

papers.abstract: Dynamics and physical state of chromatin are crucial in regulating gene expression, DNA replication, and repair. Intrinsically disordered histone tails were previously recognized as key modulators of chromatin states. However, detailed atomistic mechanisms by which histone tail dynamics are associated with chromatin compaction and higher-order chromatin organization remain poorly understood. In this work, we combine extensive all-atom molecular dynamics simulations of tri-nucleosomes with varying linker lengths and cryo-electron tomography (cryo-ET) of native nucleosome arrays. Our approach offers distinct advantages as it elucidates realistic inter-nucleosomal interactions and tri-nucleosome orientations derived from physics-based MD simulations, enabling a more accurate and physically grounded interpretation of cryo-ET data. The results reveal that tri-nucleosome models can be successfully used for fitting and the near-atomistic interpretation of cryo-ET density maps of native human chromatin. Moreover, histone tails were shown to promote chromatin compaction via three major patterns: through histone-DNA interactions, histone H2A-H4 and H3-H4 tail-tail interactions. Notably, the distributions of MD-generated structural parameters of tri-nucleosomes were found to be in strong agreement with those of experimental condensed chromatin arrays.

papers.abstract: Heart failure with preserved ejection fraction (HFpEF) accounts for over half of heart failure cases but remains poorly defined due to its clinical heterogeneity. In the prospective PACIFIC-Preserved cohort (NCT04189029, n = 155), we applied multimodal deep phenotyping, including high-throughput proteomics, and unsupervised machine learning to identify biologically distinct HFpEF subgroups. Multiview clustering revealed two major HFpEF phenogroups: PEF1, characterized by inflammatory signaling, TNF receptor activation, cardio-skeletal injury, and greater renal dysfunction; and PEF2, marked by endothelial stress and milder perturbations. Conventional diagnostics alone could not reliably distinguish these subgroups, but a multimodal classifier integrating clinical, imaging, and proteomic variables achieved high predictive accuracy (F1-score 0.87). External validation in the MEDIA-DHF cohort (n = 456) confirmed that PEF1 was independently associated with adverse outcomes (adjusted HR 2.27, 95% CI 1.04-4.94). These findings establish a classifier-driven, biologically informed stratification of HFpEF, providing a framework for precision medicine in heart failure.

papers.abstract: Targeting tumor-associated macrophages holds great promise for cancer immunotherapy. Surface glycoproteins in macrophages regulate their interactions with tumor cells and represent emerging therapeutic targets. Given the importance of glycoproteins in immunity and cancer, we systematically investigate the total and surface glycoproteomes in polarized macrophages using multiplexed proteomics coupled with selective enrichment. In monocyte-derived macrophages, distinct changes of N-glycoproteins are observed between M1 and M2 phenotypes, with more pronounced alterations in pro-inflammatory M1. In M1, glycoproteins involved in chondroitin sulfate-type glycosaminoglycan (CS-GAG) biosynthesis are upregulated, validated by the elevated CS-GAG levels, and enzymes associated with nucleotide sugar biosynthesis are also upregulated, consistent with the increased hexokinase activity. Furthermore, surface glycoproteomic analysis of primary human macrophages with M1 or M2 phenotype (HM1 and HM2) reveals phenotype-specific remodeling: HM1 display enhanced innate immune signaling, whereas surface glycoproteins related to adhesion and endocytosis are upregulated in HM2. Integrative analyses of cell-surface glycoproteomic, transcriptomic, and tissue-specific datasets enable prioritization of candidate surface proteins associated with M2 phenotype, including LIPA, CD200R1, and CR1, and phenotype-specific changes of several surface glycoproteins are validated by immunofluorescence imaging. Together, this study provides insights into macrophage functional specialization and advances our understanding of cell-surface glycoproteins.

papers.abstract: The RAS/MAPK pathway is among the most frequently dysregulated in human cancer, predominantly driven by activating mutations across RAS and BRAF in a broad spectrum of tumor types. The recent clinical validation of direct inhibitors of RAS, long considered undruggable, has reenergized the field and renewed focus on targeting the full RAS/MAPK axis. MEK, a central node in MAPK signaling, remains an attractive mutation-agnostic target, yet the efficacy of first-generation MEK inhibitors has been limited by pathway reactivation in tumors and by on-target, off-tissue toxicity. In this issue of Cancer Research, Kolitz and colleagues describe atebimetinib, a novel MEK inhibitor that also prevents feedback-induced MEK phosphorylation by RAF. The uniquely short plasma half-life of atebimetinib enables deep cyclic inhibition (DCI): transient but profound MEK/ERK output suppression with full recovery between doses. At each drug's tolerability limit, atebimetinib outperformed the MEK inhibitor binimetinib across multiple RAS- and BRAF-mutant tumor models. Whether DCI or suppression of MEK phosphorylation is the primary driver of the improved therapeutic window and how atebimetinib compares with the clinical standard and other MEK-targeting agents remain important open questions, but the work makes a compelling case that novel pharmacology can unlock therapeutic spaces at targets long considered exhausted. See related article by Kolitz et al., p. 5223.

papers.abstract: Extensive-stage small cell lung cancer (ES-SCLC) is a rare yet highly aggressive malignancy with severely limited treatment options. The efficacy of immunotherapy for ES-SCLC remain limited, with only 14% of patients deriving additional benefit from immune checkpoint inhibitors (ICIs), underscoring significant heterogeneity in patient response. This study aimed to develop a model for the accurate prediction of prognosis and therapeutic response to optimize treatment strategies. 99 and 25 ES-SCLC patients were enrolled as training and independent internal validation cohorts. Baseline CT images, clinical data, and laboratory markers were collected. Prognostic factors were screened via Cox regression. A mediastinal window CT-based deep learning model (MWDL) was developed and combined with Progastrin-releasing peptide (log(ProGRP + 1)) and bone metastasis to establish the novel MWGB-Cox model. ProGRP and bone metastasis were independent prognostic factors with area under the curves (AUCs) of 0.705 and 0.666 respectively for predicting 1-year OS. Among the pure deep learning models, the MWDL model achieved better performance with a mean AUC of 0.813 than the deep learning model based on lung window CT images (LWDL, AUC 0.756). Whereas the multimodal MWGB-Cox model not only achieved the highest AUC (0.902) for 1-year OS prediction, but also effectively overcame the limitation of insufficient sensitivity. The predictive performance of the MWGB-Cox model was further validated in the independent internal validation cohort. This novel, simple, and cost-effective multimodal MWGB-Cox model integrating CT-based deep learning, log(ProGRP + 1), and bone metastasis could robustly predict 1-year OS of ES-SCLC patients receiving first-line immunotherapy, providing a reliable tool for clinical decision-making. By integrating CT-based deep learning, log(ProGRP + 1) levels, and bone metastasis, the novel multimodal model achieved the highest predictive AUC (0.902) with improved sensitivity, serving as a simple, cost-effective tool for clinical decision-making.

papers.abstract: Patient-centred precision care [(PC) 2 ] is a new paradigm in anaesthesia that applies individualised care principles to tailor perioperative care to individual patient characteristics, preferences, and values. This individualised strategy aims to optimise anaesthetic effectiveness, minimise side effects, and align care with what matters most to patients – whether survival, cognitive preservation, pain control, or rapid functional recovery. By considering elements such as genetics, comorbidities, environmental influences, and lifestyle, (PC) 2 improves outcomes and fosters long-term health and cost-effectiveness. Despite its promise, implementing (PC) 2 faces challenges. Healthcare systems often prioritise efficiency over individualisation, while clinicians may focus on short-term outcomes. Regulatory hurdles and fragmented stakeholder input sometimes hinder industry efforts. To guide practical application, we present 12 practice recommendations for integrating (PC) 2 into routine anaesthesia practice. These recommendations were derived from our experience implementing (PC) 2 approaches, including Enhanced Recovery After Surgery, the Safe Brain Initiative, and the Brain Health Initiative. We also highlight the importance of evidence-based practice, health economic awareness, pragmatic clinical solutions, and the development of continuous quality improvement processes to promote sustainable excellence in care. Together, these strategies offer a roadmap for clinicians and organisations to deliver more precise, patient-specific, and effective anaesthesia, ultimately leading to better perioperative outcomes and experiences. Successful adoption of (PC) 2 in real-world practice requires systemic alignment, a feedback-oriented culture, and active leadership engagement. This review highlights that these organisational elements are crucial for implementing (PC) 2 across diverse healthcare settings.

papers.abstract: Single-cell sequencing offers profound insights into tumor complexity. However, reliably linking individual cellular profiles to overall sample-level phenotypes remains computationally challenging, particularly when cell-specific annotations are absent. This disconnect limits the technology's utility in studying underlying tumor mechanisms. Here we show how scTransMIL, an artificial intelligence framework, bridges this gap. By conceptualizing a biological sample as a collection of individual cells, scTransMIL employs a transformer-based multi-instance learning approach to directly connect single-cell transcriptomic profiles with overarching sample-level labels. We demonstrate that scTransMIL accurately predicts sample-level cancer phenotypes, including the tissue-of-origin for metastatic tumors. At cellular resolution, it robustly identifies tumor-associated cell populations and maps biological progression trajectories using only minimal sample-level annotations. Furthermore, the model's attention mechanisms facilitate full-transcriptome biomarker discovery. By systematically integrating molecular and cellular scales with broader phenotypic states, our approach provides a computational tool to dissect tumor heterogeneity and advance fundamental cancer biology.

papers.abstract: GRN haploinsufficiency reduces progranulin and causes frontotemporal dementia (FTD-GRN). VES001, an oral small-molecule sortilin inhibitor, increases progranulin without downregulating sortilin. Preclinically, VES001 bound sortilin selectively and elevated progranulin in plasma, cerebrospinal fluid (CSF), and hippocampal interstitial fluid of male rats. In a randomized, double-blind, placebo-controlled first-in-human phase 1 A study, 79 healthy adults (63/37% male/female; mean age 28 years) received VES001 or placebo as single ascending doses (10-990 mg) or multiple ascending doses for 7 days (180 mg once or twice daily, or 450 mg twice daily). Safety and tolerability, the primary endpoints, were met: no deaths, serious adverse events or treatment-related discontinuations; headache and fatigue were mild and not dose-related. Pharmacokinetics were dose-proportional, with blood-brain barrier penetration. Prespecified pharmacodynamic endpoints were met as single dosing increased plasma progranulin, and twice-daily dosing produced greater, sustained increases versus placebo in plasma (peak 49% change from baseline) and CSF (18% change from baseline). Although cohorts were small, dosing lasted 7 days, and participants were healthy, these findings establish pharmacological proof of mechanism for oral sortilin inhibition and support further development of VES001 as a potential disease-modifying therapy for FTD-GRN. papers.abstract: High-grade gliomas carry a poor prognosis, and MRI-based radiotherapy (RT) planning may inadequately capture metabolically active tumor infiltration. ¹⁸F-fluoroethyl-tyrosine (FET) PET provides superior tumor delineation, yet prospective North American evidence supporting integration with RT planning remains limited. FETSMaRT enrolled 30 patients with WHO grade 3 or 4 high-grade glioma receiving post-operative RT. FET-PET/MRI was acquired before RT with the radiation oncologist blinded to PET, enabling retrospective quantification of discordance between MRI-based and FET-PET/MRI-derived gross tumor (GTV), clinical target (CTV), and planning target (PTV) volumes. In the glioblastoma subgroup (n = 23), Kaplan-Meier and Cox analyses related GTV and CTV discordance to time to progression. Median age was 60 years; 77% had glioblastoma and 60% MGMT promoter methylation. GTV discordance occurred in 17/30 patients (56.7%) and CTV discordance in 15/30 (50.0%). FET-PET/MRI-derived volumes significantly exceeded MRI-based volumes for GTV (43.6 vs. 38.6 cc; p < 0.0001), CTV (119.2 vs. 110.8 cc; p = 0.0045), and PTV (171.1 vs. 159.6 cc; p = 0.0003). Larger GTV∆ and CTV∆ change values were associated with numerically shorter median time to progression, but neither association was statistically significant. Radiation treatment failures were predominantly central (60.0%). FET-PET/MRI-derived target volumes were significantly larger than MRI-based volumes, confirming systematic underestimation of metabolically active tumor extent by anatomical MRI. While not meeting significance in this pilot study, directional CTV and GTV discordance suggests a possible association with progression; the hypothesis generating exploratory pilot data nonetheless justify a prospective trial of FET-PET-guided RT in high-grade glioma. papers.abstract: Central neurocytomas (CNs) are rare, WHO grade 2 brain tumors that have relatively high recurrence rates following resection. The present collaboration between Northwestern University and the Mayo Clinic describes long-term outcomes of CN as it relates to potential prognostic variables that entail recurrence risk, such as RT timing, tumor proliferation index (Ki-67), and age at diagnosis. Patients established between 1990 and 2025 with a tissue diagnosis of CN were reviewed. Recurrence free survival (RFS) and overall survival (OS) were calculated according to the Kaplan Meier-method. Multivariate cox regression analysis was performed with pre-planned variables. Fifty-one patients with CN with a median age of 26 years and 9.7 years median follow-up were included. OS at 10 years for the cohort was 94%. Without adjuvant RT, 5-year RFS for post-GTR was 61% versus 46% for post-STR (P value = 0.18). Multivariate analysis found omission of adjuvant RT (HR: 9.0, P = 0.003), subtotal resection (HR:5.7, P = 0.017), younger age at diagnosis (HR3.1, P = 0.002), and higher Ki-67 (HR 1.13, P = 0.017) were associated with worse RFS. Salvage RT after first recurrence (n = 17) had a 5-year RFS of 83%, with a median follow-up of 4.8 years. We report one of the largest and most comprehensive cohorts of CN with long-term follow-up. Contrary to previous reports, recurrences were frequent after GTR. Higher Ki-67 and age at diagnosis were associated with worse RFS in our cohort. Salvage RT at recurrence achieved durable long-term tumor control, and 10-year mortality was low.

papers.abstract: Adjuvant radiotherapy (RT) following breast-conserving surgery reduces local recurrence but can introduce reconstructive morbidity. Although recent trials support the safe omission of RT in selected patients, its impact on surgical and patient-reported outcomes following oncoplastic breast-conserving surgery (OPBCS) remains poorly defined. We evaluated surgical and long-term patient-reported outcomes in patients undergoing OPBCS, stratified by receipt of RT. We retrospectively studied consecutive patients who underwent OPBCS between 2017 and 2024 for stage 0-3 breast cancer. Patients were stratified based on receipt of RT. Postoperative complications, unplanned reoperation, and revision procedures were compared between cohorts. Long-term patient-reported outcomes were assessed using the validated BREAST-Q Reconstruction Module. Multivariable regression was used to evaluate the independent association between RT status and outcomes. We identified 257 patients; 210 patients received RT (81.7%) and 47 underwent RT de-escalation (18.3%). Surgical site infection (p = 0.100), delayed wound healing (p = 0.300), and skin flap necrosis rates (p = 0.0300) were similar between cohorts. Seroma (30% vs. 13%; p = 0.006) and unplanned reoperation (21% vs. 7.1%; p = 0.006) were more frequent with RT omission. Patients who did not receive RT demonstrated significantly higher mean Satisfaction with Breasts scores compared with those who received RT (57 ± 25 vs. 23 ± 24; p = 0.001). In adjusted models, RT de-escalation was associated with a 36-point increase in Satisfaction with Breasts scores (β = 36.0; 95% CI, 18.0-54.0; p < 0.001). RT omission was independently associated with higher patient-reported satisfaction with breasts, though patients had higher seroma and reoperation rates. These data support balanced shared decision-making for RT de-escalation in appropriately selected patients.

papers.abstract: Acute lymphoblastic leukemia (ALL) exhibits molecular and metabolic heterogeneity that limits therapeutic efficacy. Although antimetabolites remain central to ALL treatment, determinants of therapeutic sensitivity and resistance remain incompletely understood. Here, we investigated the activity and molecular response landscape of the purine analog triciribine (TCN) across diverse ALL models using integrated phosphoproteomics, thermal proteome profiling, and quantitative proteomics. TCN showed potent cytotoxicity across ALL cell lines and a drug response profile distinct from canonical PI3K-Akt-mTOR inhibitors. Early phosphoproteomics revealed no consistent suppression of Akt pathway signaling, with transient activation of several Akt-associated readouts and inhibition of cyclin-dependent kinase signaling. The monophosphorylated metabolite TCN-P was the predominant intracellular active species, and adenosine kinase (ADK) was required for TCN-P generation and cytotoxicity. Proteome Integral Solubility Alteration profiling identified candidate TCN-P interactions involving nucleotide metabolism, DNA replication, and protein synthesis, associated with impaired purine biosynthesis, DNA damage, translational stress, and cell-cycle perturbation. Across ALL cell lines and primary samples, ADK levels correlated positively with TCN sensitivity, supporting ADK-dependent metabolism as a major determinant of therapeutic response. Together, these findings identify TCN as a metabolically activated antileukemic agent with broad antimetabolite activity and nominate ADK as a potential predictive biomarker for precision therapy in ALL.

papers.abstract: Early identification of vulnerable carotid plaques is crucial for stroke prevention, but the upstream metabolic processes linked to endothelial transition and immune recruitment remain poorly defined. We characterised lactate metabolism in ACKR1+ endothelial cells (ECs) in human carotid plaques and derived a machine-learning signature for discriminating plaque vulnerability. Internal and external (GSE253903) single-cell datasets were integrated to identify endothelial subpopulations, and bulk transcriptomic (GSE163154) and in-house proteomic data were used to assess metabolism-immune correlations. Least absolute shrinkage and selection operator (LASSO) regression selected core features for a logistic model, which was locked and applied to three independent cohorts: GSE43292 (Stary stage ≥ IV vs. I-II), GSE28829 (early vs. advanced lesions) and GSE100927 (normal vs. atherosclerotic arteries). Key molecules were validated in situ by immunohistochemistry (IHC) and spatial transcriptomics in independent plaques (five stable, five unstable). An ACKR1+ EC subpopulation linked to neovascularisation showed hyperactive glycolysis and enhanced lactate metabolism. Computational inference linked lactate accumulation to HIF-1α stability, CXCL12 release and CD8+ T-cell infiltration via the CXCL12-CXCR4 axis, and the monocarboxylate transporters SLC16A3 and SLC16A4 emerged as quantitative readouts of this 'lactate-immune' state. In unstable plaques, IHC confirmed higher atypical chemokine receptor 1 (ACKR1; geometric mean ratio [GMR] = 6.82), CD8+ T-cell density (GMR = 4.63), SLC16A3 (GMR = 4.74) and HIF-1α (GMR = 4.02; all q < .05), with lactylation elevated in the lipid core. A four-feature model (ACKR1, SLC16A3, SLC16A4, CD8+ T-cell cytotoxicity score) performed well in training and retained discrimination in the progression-stratified cohorts, while in GSE100927 it showed high disease-identification performance across three arterial beds. Lactate metabolic reprogramming under hypoxia is associated with ACKR1+ EC-related CD8+ T-cell recruitment and plaque instability. This chain is an association-based hypothesis requiring functional confirmation. The signature discriminates robustly at both the vulnerability-stratification and disease-identification levels, providing a quantifiable framework for molecular classification of atherosclerotic plaques.

papers.abstract: The ubiquitous availability of protein structures permits replacing sequence alignment with more accurate and sensitive structure alignment algorithms. LoL-align maximizes a local log-odds score for proteins to be homologous, given their intra-protein Cα - Cα distances. Here we show that LoL-align is markedly more sensitive in detecting remote homologs than TM-align and Dali on single- and multidomain benchmarks and achieves better alignment quality at 5-20 × their speed. LoL-align is fully integrated into Foldseek.

papers.abstract: Preterm birth is associated with breakdown of maternal-fetal tolerance and remains the leading cause of global mortality in young children. However, the role of self-reactive antibodies has been limited to a handful of pathogenic allo- and autoantibodies linked to pregnancy complications. Here we identify a shared autoreactive signature of pregnancy in pregnant sera (n = 2,719) relative to never-pregnant controls (n = 130), using proteome-wide autoantibody profiling. Across eight human pregnancy cohorts, we define autoreactivities associated with preterm birth by comparing preterm (n = 688) and term (n = 1,505) pregnancies. Within the signature, antibodies to IL1 receptor antagonist (IL1RA) induce resorption, inflammation and vascular malperfusion in pregnant mice. IL1RA localizes to placental endothelial adherens junctions, suggesting a role in vascular integrity. These findings identify a term pregnancy humoral immune program and shared changes preceding preterm delivery, including anti-IL1RA, which may have direct pathogenic consequences.

papers.abstract: The 2025 M7.8 Mandalay earthquake ruptured ~480 km of the Sagaing Fault, producing one of the longest strike-slip events documented and impacting a vulnerable region. Here we combine remote sensing observations and numerical modeling to show that the subsurface fault geometry and slip distribution could be anticipated from pre-event observations. Along-strike variations in coseismic and interseismic deformation reveal a helix-shaped fault geometry. The average coseismic slip equals or exceeds the interseismic slip deficit, consistent with a minimally slip-predictable model. We generate an ensemble of 3D dynamic rupture models, constrained by the best-fit static slip model, then discriminate among them using independent space-geodetic, seismic, and near-field video observations. The preferred scenario begins bilaterally, then transitions to unilateral southward supershear propagation at depth, while shallow rupture remains subshear. These dynamics are shaped by localized stress heterogeneity and low fracture energy, characteristic of a structurally mature fault zone. Our approach can inform rupture scenarios in understudied regions.

papers.abstract: The HK97-fold is an ancient, conserved protein structure that assembles protein shells, forming the capsids of Duplodnaviria viruses and prokaryotic biochemical compartments called encapsulsins. It has been proposed that encapsulins evolved from HK97-fold viruses. But the higher complexity of viral capsids represents a biophysical paradox in the evolution of HK97-fold protein shells. To resolve this problem, we hypothesize the existence of simpler HK97-fold viral capsids associated with smaller genomes than those of known HK97-fold viruses. Such small viral genomes are searched in environmental metagenomes across public databases, including IMG/M and MGnify. Using hidden Markov models and protein language models, we identify and characterize small viral genomes encoding HK97-fold proteins that exhibit molecular similarities to encapsulins yet lack portal and tail genes. The phylogenetic analyses of HK97-fold proteins reveal independent mixed groups of viruses and encapsulins, and structural analyses identify similarities between encapsulins and procapsids, the immature state of viral capsids. The observations support a bidirectional evolution between encapsulins and HK97-fold viruses enabled by the viral procapsid state. Using biophysical and genomic arguments, we introduce an evolutionary model of HK97-fold protein shells, predicting that they emerged as lower-symmetry biochemical compartments and that HK97-fold viral capsids may retain biochemical functions.

papers.abstract: Heterogeneous crystallization kinetics critically govern the morphology and performance of solution-processed semiconductors, yet morphology control is often achieved through trial-and-error optimization. Quantitative understanding of crystallization is essential for precise morphology control but is limited by the simultaneous occurrence of heterogeneous nucleation and crystal growth. Here, a time-defined induced nucleation strategy has been developed to initiate crystallization at specific stages of solution processing. Systematic variation of nucleation timing reveals three distinct morphological regimes, whose emergence is explained by the concentration-dependent critical cluster radius in bulk, interfacial, and cusp environments. On this basis, a quantitative, dimensionless model is developed for heterogeneous crystallization kinetics across diverse processing conditions. The model demonstrates universality across perovskite and organic semiconductors. In situ studies reveal identical growth kinetics for induced and spontaneous nuclei, validating its generality. The resulting morphology control enables tuning of crystallinity and charge transport in solution-processed transistors.

papers.abstract: Hydroformylation has been a cornerstone of industrial organometallic catalysis, with regioselectivity being a critical aspect in this process1,2. Present industrial systems use homogeneous Rh-based catalysts with expensive and toxic phosphine-containing ligands, underscoring the need to develop alternative heterogeneous catalysts that could compete with the actual homogeneous ones3. In this direction, atomically dispersed Rh catalysts have been proposed as promising candidates for hydroformylation4,5. However, achieving high regioselectivity at high conversion is still a big challenge. Here subnanometre Rh2O3 clusters are confined inside the channels of the MFI zeolite, which under reaction conditions disrupt into isolated Rh3+ and Rh+ species. Density functional theory (DFT) investigations combined with spectroscopic and catalytic studies demonstrate that Rh3+-mediated hydroformylation is energetically plausibly similar to Rh+, with Rh3+ being intrinsically more selective for hydroformylation and less selective for double-bond isomerization than Rh+. In the coexistence of both Rh3+ and Rh+ species, we demonstrate the possibility to selectively inhibit Rh+ sites through the addition of N-containing molecules such as N-methylpyrrolidine (MP) or 1-methyl-2-pyrrolidone (NMP), which preferentially coordinate to Rh+ inside MFI zeolite channel, thereby suppressing its isomerization function while leaving Rh3+ sites catalytically accessible. This strategy results in a notable enhancement of regioselectivity, with a state-of-the-art reported highest linear to branched aldehydes (l/b) ratio of 817 with 96% undecanal selectivity at 99.8% 1-decene conversion, using NMP as additive.

papers.abstract: De novo design of enzymes that cleave amide bonds represents a major challenge1,2. Here we use RFdiffusion methods3,4 to de novo design proteins with water-activating zinc-based active sites adjacent to a peptide substrate binding pocket. Of 135 designs tested, 36% catalyse cleavage of their cognate peptide substrates at the targeted scissile bond. The best design accelerates peptide-bond hydrolysis by more than 108-fold relative to the uncatalysed reaction; four substitutions increase this acceleration to more than 1010-fold by improving active-site preorganization5. We use this approach to design metalloproteases that selectively cleave the human disease-associated proteins TDP-43, amyloid-β and serum amyloid A, with rate enhancements of up to 109-fold. We further design caged cytokines and receptor antagonists that are selectively activated by the designed proteases, enabling bioorthogonal control of cell state. Thus, de novo design can yield highly active, programmable proteases with applications in therapeutics, biotechnology and bioremediation.

papers.abstract: Despite advances in de novo enzyme design, success has been largely limited to low-energy-barrier model reactions. Amide bonds such as those linking amino acids along the peptide backbone are stable for hundreds of years in neutral aqueous solution because of the high energy barrier to hydrolysis1. Here we describe the de novo design of enzymes that use an activated cysteine nucleophile to hydrolyse the polypeptide backbone in a sequence-dependent manner, with a success rate of 13/69 = 19% and rate enhancements over the background reaction (kcat/kuncat) of up to 3 × 107. The designed proteases have folds that are very different from proteases in nature (TM score < 0.50), and six crystal structures are very close to the design models (Cα root mean squared deviation of <1.2 Å), highlighting the capacity for generalization and the accuracy of the design methodology. Experimental and computational analyses suggest that the remaining gap in activity to the most active native cysteine proteases arises from imperfections in active-site preorganization and substrate positioning. The designed proteases efficiently cleave their targets in mammalian cells, opening the door to a wide range of synthetic biology applications.

papers.abstract: Astrocytomas and oligodendrogliomas are isocitrate dehydrogenase (IDH)-mutant gliomas that most commonly arise in adults under the age of 50 and exhibit variable responses to treatment1-3. To understand the genetic drivers of disease progression, here we used whole-genome and whole-exome sequencing to characterize longitudinally collected tumour specimens from 183 patients with IDH-mutant glioma. Samples were collected through the Glioma Longitudinal Analysis (GLASS) Consortium4. Most primary surgery samples were classified as grade 2 on the basis of histology (73% for astrocytomas and 93% for oligodendrogliomas). We validated known genomic markers of tumour progression, including hypermutation and homozygous deletion of CDKN2A or CDKN2B (hereafter, CDKN2A/B)5, and discovered genetic alterations that distinguish between the evolutionary trajectories of astrocytomas and those of oligodendrogliomas. Mutations in phosphatidylinositol 3-kinase (PI3K) and NOTCH1 were newly acquired in recurrent oligodendrogliomas, regardless of treatment, and were associated with an increased tumour mutational burden. In recurrent astrocytomas, however, again irrespective of treatment, acquired focal oncogene amplifications and CDKN2A/B homozygous deletions were associated with an increase in chromosomal imbalances, which converged with markers of chromosomal instability such as chromothripsis and whole-genome doubling. In both types of IDH-mutant glioma, we observed a convergence of acquired alterations, genome-wide changes and worse patient outcomes, suggesting that treatment-refractory clones were being selected. Treatment with temozolomide was associated with the mutational signatures SBS11 and SBS119 in both tumour types, whereas the radiotherapy-associated ID8 signature increased in astrocytomas specifically. We show that the genomes of oligodendrogliomas and astrocytomas adapt to the selective pressures of tumour progression and treatment in distinct ways, suggesting that oligodendrogliomas and astrocytomas differ in their responses to treatment-induced DNA damage.

papers.abstract: In acute myocardial infarction and acute kidney injury, capillary no-reflow denotes that capillary blood flow is still blocked despite successful arterial reperfusion. This is associated with substantially increased mortality and reinfarction risk; nevertheless, no targeted therapy exists so far1,2. Because capillary no-reflow is driven by smooth muscle myosin-mediated hypercontraction of capillary pericytes, we developed R(+)2501, a myosin-specific and capillary-selective vasodilator. In reperfused animal models of acute myocardial infarction and acute kidney injury, direct in vivo imaging showed that R(+)2501 rapidly restored capillary flow, an effect sustained even after rapid drug clearance. Ex vivo experiments confirmed reversal of pericyte constriction directly. Restoration of capillary blood flow, together with clearance of trapped neutrophils, linked resolution of capillary no-reflow to attenuation of an early driver of reperfusion injury. R(+)2501 enhanced capillary perfusion while preserving coronary autoregulation and systemic haemodynamics, and markedly improved survival during acute reperfusion. We further found that acute myocardial infarction induced renal capillary no-reflow, which was reversed by R(+)2501, suggesting that capillary no-reflow contributes to the pathophysiology of cardiorenal syndrome type I. These findings establish pericyte-targeted smooth muscle myosin inhibition as a therapeutic strategy to restore microvascular perfusion and halt the ischaemic cascade across organs, while defining a specific physiological role for capillaries and pericytes in circulatory regulation.

papers.abstract: During the execution of learned motor skills, the neural population in layer 2/3 (L2/3) of primary motor cortex (M1) expresses a reproducible spatiotemporal activity pattern1. It is debated whether M1 actively participates in generating this learned pattern and whether this pattern causally drives the learned movement2-5. Here we combined in vivo two-photon calcium imaging and holographic optogenetic stimulation of functionally defined M1 L2/3 ensembles in mice performing a skilled lever-pressing task. Brief synchronous stimulation of about 20 neurons whose activity onset precedes voluntary movement onset induced movements resembling the learned movement, while producing activity patterns in other M1 neurons resembling the learned activity. Moreover, trial-by-trial variability of optogenetically triggered population activity correlated with variability in the induced movements. These variabilities were predicted by the initial state of M1 activity preceding stimulation. In some trials, stimulation induced the learned activity without inducing movements, indicating that the learned activity is not simply a reflection of movements but can arise internally. Stimulation failed to generate movements or learned activity in task-disengaged mice. Stimulation of neurons whose activity followed movement onsets failed to induce the learned movement in task-engaged mice. Together, the learned activity in M1 L2/3 can be generated when M1 is prepared at the optimal initial state and receives precise triggering inputs, supporting the active role of M1 in generating learned activity and learned movements.
