papers.abstract: The ability to faithfully initiate embryogenesis from a single, induced non-germline cell type, akin to the totipotent blastomeres, remains a considerable challenge in developmental and synthetic biology1-14. Here we established conditions that enable the continuous ex utero development of mouse embryo models (EMs), starting solely from the chemically induced totipotent-like stem cells (ciTotiSCs)15 and spanning the pre-implantation morula, blastocysts and post-gastrulation stages with both embryonic and extraembryonic compartments. These ciTotiSCs self-organized into blastocyst-like structures that closely resembled natural blastocysts in both morphology and lineage segregation. The resulting ciTotiSC-derived EMs (ciToti-EMs) successfully progressed through key developmental milestones, including gastrulation, embryonic axis formation, haematopoiesis and early organogenesis, closely resembling embryonic day 8.5 (E8.5) natural embryos (NEs). Furthermore, extended culture led to the development of functional cardiac tissues in ciToti-EMs, highly comparable to those of E10.5 NEs. These findings demonstrate an extraordinary ability of a single induced cell type, ciTotiSCs, to autonomously recapitulate the complete spectrum of early mouse embryogenesis. Our ciToti-EM system provides a powerful model for investigating mammalian embryonic development and opens new avenues for creating multicellular organisms from non-germline cells.

papers.abstract: Conservation areas are critical for tackling the global environmental crisis1. These sites are reported as covering 18.5% of the terrestrial realm2 and governments have committed through Global Biodiversity Framework Target 3 to increase this to at least 30% by 2030 (ref. 3). There are concerns that this potential near-doubling of conservation area coverage will negatively affect vulnerable people and over-stretch conservation resources4. However, nationally available datasets indicate that more conservation areas exist than are reflected in global figures5-7. We evaluated progress towards the area component of Target 3 using a globally representative sample across 25 countries and territories that incorporated these national datasets8. Extrapolating from this sample, we show that conservation areas likely already cover 26.81% of the terrestrial realm. We may be much closer to achieving 30% terrestrial coverage than previously thought. However, we also show that the extra land does not substantially address gaps in ecological representativeness, indicating that solely meeting the area component of Target 3 will do little to solve continuing global biodiversity loss. More focus and resources are needed to achieve the other components of the target, using a more strategic and inclusive approach to fill present gaps and produce equitable and effective conservation area networks.

papers.abstract: When metals are magnetized1, emulsions phase separate2, or galaxies cluster3, domain walls and patterns form and irremediably coarsen over time. This coarsening is universally driven by diffusive relaxation towards equilibrium. Here we discover a vibrational counterpart-wave coarsening-in active elastic media4-13: vibrations emerge and spontaneously grow in wavelength, period and amplitude, before a globally synchronized state called a time crystal14-17 forms. We observe wave coarsening in one- and two-dimensional mechatronic metamaterials and capture its dynamical scaling. We further arrest the process by breaking momentum conservation and reveal a far-from-equilibrium nonlinear analogue to chiral topological edge modes18-24. Our results open new questions about the transient physics of systems with non-potential interactions15,25-28 and suggest an organizing principle for nonlinear waves in acoustics29,30, optomechanics31,32, living matter6,33 and soft robotics9.

papers.abstract: The global monsoon system provides freshwater to much of Earth's biota, including its human population1. The Milankovitch theory predicts changes in Earth's solar insolation over geologic time, and these variations are expected to result in changes to the global monsoon2. Internal climate forcings, such as ice cover and sea surface temperatures, may also affect the system. However, few records of monsoon variability in the Southern Hemisphere over glacial-interglacial cycles exist to test our understanding of the factors that drive variations in the global monsoon. Here we show that monsoons in both the Southern and Northern Hemispheres vary with Milankovitch forcing, and with internal boundary conditions over the past 450,000 years. We present a record of South American Summer Monsoon (SASM) variability, based on speleothem oxygen-isotope data from the Amazon Basin. South American Summer Monsoon variability and that of a major Northern Hemisphere monsoon-that is, the Asian monsoon3,4-have been strikingly out of phase. However, we observe occasional synchronous behaviour in regions impacted by both monsoons. We identify a synchronicity threshold that is exceeded during ten events, including during glacial terminations. Comparison with palaeoclimatic forcing factors during these intervals indicates that greenhouse gas concentrations, cross-equatorial thermal gradients and sea surface temperatures in both the Atlantic and Pacific probably influence these events. This record demonstrates that the global monsoon can reorganize itself, especially during intervals of rapidly changing planetary boundary conditions.

papers.abstract: Interleukin-10 (IL-10) is a central anti-inflammatory cytokine that suppresses immune responses in myeloid cells but can also activate T cells, limiting its therapeutic use in chronic inflammatory diseases owing to narrow efficacy windows and dose-limiting toxicities1-5. Here we show that myeloid and T cells differ in their dependence on JAK-family kinase pairing for IL-10 signalling and function. We took advantage of this differential kinase dependence to engineer a tetravalent nanobody-based myeloid-selective IL-10 receptor agonist (msIL-10R agonist) that fully recapitulates IL-10's potent suppression of monocytes, macrophages and dendritic cells while avoiding stimulation of T cells. Cryo-electron microscopy structural analysis reveals a distinct receptor cross-linking geometry of the msIL-10R agonist compared with native IL-10 family cytokines. This tetravalent architecture renders signalling strictly TYK2-dependent and highly sensitive to IL-10Rα and IL-10Rβ receptor abundance, thereby conferring selective activity in myeloid cells. This msIL-10R agonist reduces inflammation in humanized mouse models of lipopolysaccharide challenge, delayed-type hypersensitivity and colitis. A humanized version exhibits IgG-like pharmacokinetics, sustained receptor occupancy and durable myeloid suppression up to 30 days without T cell activation or haematological toxicities in non-human primates. These findings establish a geometry-based strategy for achieving cell-type-selective cytokine signalling and identify the msIL-10R agonist as a therapeutic candidate for myeloid-driven inflammatory diseases, including inflammatory bowel diseases.

papers.abstract: Tetrapods arose from lobe-finned fishes with a notochord-dominated axial column1-3. During this transition, the skull became separated from the shoulder girdle4-6, giving rise to a neck region. This head-shoulder separation has generated hypotheses suggesting that neck mobility increased during the origin of tetrapods, facilitating the ecological transition towards more terrestrial habitats4,5,7-9. However, incompletely co-ossified vertebral components10 have posed a challenge to modelling the mobility of these early tetrapod necks. Here we used material tests on the similarly configured axial columns of sturgeon to predict the capacities of the tetrapod neck region for lateral flexion, extension and rotation across the tetrapod stem. Our model indicates that the soft tissue-dominated axial column was surprisingly rigid, despite lacking co-ossified vertebral components. We estimate that most stem tetrapods could move their heads less than 6° laterally and less than 3° dorsally but could not rotate them. Notably, mobility did not shift in conjunction with the head-shoulder separation that occurred between the origin of tristichopterids (represented by Eusthenopteron) and that of more crownward stem tetrapods. Therefore, mobility in the tetrapod neck did not serve as a functional driver of head-shoulder separation. Instead, forelimb-driven locomotion, implicated in early tetrapods11-14, provides a better functional explanation for the head-shoulder separation.

papers.abstract: The origin and early diversification of birds remain highly debated in vertebrate evolution. Although estimates of the evolutionary timescales suggest a Jurassic period radiation1,2, a profound scarcity of fossils from this period has hampered how the distinctive bird bauplan was assembled3-5. Selection for powered flight has been viewed as the primary driver of early avialan skeletal modifications3,6,7, attesting to the independent occurrences of aerodynamic features among paravian lineages8. Here we report on the discovery of a Late Jurassic avialan, Yuezhuornis yangyuanensis, gen. et sp. nov., from the Zhenghe Fauna of southeastern China9. As one of the earliest diverging avialans, Y. yangyuanensis exhibits a striking mosaic of features, combining a mixture of avialan- and troodontid-like cranial characters, paired with derived postcranial traits and a deinonychosaur-like hyperextensible second pedal digit. Phylogenetically informed analyses show that Y. yangyuanensis possesses markedly short forelimbs-a condition present widely among non-avialan theropods. These findings provide strong evidence for a terrestrial, flightless lifestyle of Y. yangyuanensis. Our study demonstrates that evolution works intensively as exemplified by the occurrence of several, divergent ecological pathways being exploited in the initial diversification of birds.

papers.abstract: Perovskite light-emitting diodes (PeLEDs) have emerged as a promising class of solution-processed light-emitting devices, combining high efficiency with facile fabrication1-5. Amino-acid-based molecular additives are widely used to regulate crystallization and suppress defects in perovskite thin films6-8, yet these molecules are chemically reactive in precursor solutions, in which their transformations and products remain poorly understood. Here we resolve and control the hidden solution-phase chemistry of a ubiquitous additive, 5-aminovaleric acid (5AVA), whose solution-phase reactivity has remained unclear6,9-15. We show that 5AVA undergoes competing in situ reactions during precursor preconditioning, yielding two chemically and functionally distinct products: a beneficial organoamidinium zwitterion and a detrimental Lewis-base lactam. By explaining this reaction dichotomy and establishing targeted reaction-pathway control, we selectively use the beneficial species. Direct synthesis and incorporation of the purified zwitterion decouple its intrinsic passivation function from confounding by-products, yielding perovskite films with a near-unity mean peak photoluminescence quantum yield (PLQY) of 97.2% and PeLEDs with a champion external quantum efficiency (EQE) of 37.1%, alongside a mean peak EQE of 32.8%. Finally, we demonstrate that this reaction-pathway control concept can be extended to further additive chemistries and emission colours, highlighting its potential as a chemistry-driven strategy for rational additive design in PeLEDs.

papers.abstract: In lithium-ion batteries, the bulk solvation structure of the electrolyte is a major determinant of the physical and electrochemical properties of the cell, for example, conductivity, viscosity, salt dissociation and subsequent reactivity, the electrochemical stability window (and thus solid electrolyte interphase formation), and the composition of the electrochemical double layer1-3. However, elucidation of this structure at an atomic level of detail has been challenging to accomplish via a purely experimental approach. Here we combine machine-learning-enabled atomistic simulations4-16, nuclear magnetic resonance spectroscopy, electrochemical data3,17-20 and quantum-chemical calculations to reveal previously unstudied multi-Li+ complexes without bound anions that are uniquely facile for reduction. This insight explains the success of empirically chosen ethylene-carbonate-containing solvent mixtures and provides a foundation for the rational design of improved electrolytes. Furthermore, our machine-learning force-field-based lithium-ion-battery electrolyte simulations accurately reproduce a wide range of condensed-phase experiments3,21-24, despite being parameterized to only quantum-chemical gas-phase cluster calculations, and hence provide a compelling demonstration that machine-learning force-field-based models developed from first principles can robustly represent a complex chemical system to atomic resolution.

papers.abstract: Two-dimensional graphene sheets show strong potential for use in fabrication of macroscopic films, as they have exceptional mechanical properties owing to their in-plane strength1-6. Improvements in the stacking order of flat two-dimensional sheets have led to corresponding improvements in the strength and toughness of such films7-11. In addition, modulation of the spatial conformation of individual units has enabled the development of benchmark materials with superior properties12,13; however, this has remained elusive in the case of two-dimensional sheets. Here we report a strategy for preparation of graphene films with a combination of high strength (2.9 GPa), toughness (84.5 MJ m-3) and elastic strain (5%). We attribute these performance gains to a fold-clasping lamellar structure achieved by modular assembly of surface-folded multilayer graphene oxide flakes. We identify a pull-to-push transition of force chain topology and propose a shear-lock stress transfer strategy in the fold-clasping lamellar graphene film that enables advances in mechanical properties. This work demonstrates the modular design of spatial conformation of two-dimensional flakes on a large scale and further improves the performance of macroscopic films for potential applications in lightweight structural components.

papers.abstract: Collective behaviour in quantum materials can produce excitations carrying only a fraction of the quantum numbers of their constituents. A notable case occurs in chains of spin-1 units1, in which a topological gap protects the interior of the chain, whereas spin-1/2 states, half the spin of the units that form it, emerge at the ends2. In short chains, these fractional edge spins couple to each other and their topological protection makes them attractive for hybrid spin-superconductor devices. Whether such fractionalization survives the proximity of a superconducting condensate, however, remains an open question. Here we grow molecular Haldane chains of antiferromagnetically coupled spin-1 triangulene units on a proximitized Au(111)/Nb(110) surface and resolve a parity-dependent coupling of their spin-1/2 edge states to the superconductor by scanning tunnelling spectroscopy. Odd-length chains host Yu-Shiba-Rusinov (YSR) bound states inside the superconducting gap, originating from a global S = 1 ground state, whereas even-length chains form an S = 0 ground state decoupled from the superconductor. A two-site model attributes this alternation to the sign and strength of inter-edge interactions, independently confirmed by extra-gap spin excitations in tunnelling spectra. Many-body spin excitations of the S = 1 chain are also detected, decoupled from the superconductor by the much larger Haldane gap. The length-tunable coupling of the edge spins to superconductors opens a route towards molecular spin qubits based on π-conjugated carbon architectures.

papers.abstract: Space-based remote sensing allows detection and monitoring of large, concentrated methane sources worldwide1. However, independent evaluation of instruments and algorithms is limited, and new satellites and artificial intelligence techniques have not been tested under controlled, single-blind conditions2. Here we conduct a year-long, single-blind test involving 746 events: 481 methane releases of 9.5-1,183.7 kg h-1 and 265 blank controls. We released metered methane quantities in Arizona, USA, coinciding with overpasses from 12 government, commercial and non-profit satellites. Fifteen analysis teams from nine countries generated more than 2,250 estimates, making this, to our knowledge, the largest controlled test so far and one of the first evaluations of the instruments EMIT, Tanager-1 (Carbon Mapper) and GHOSt. Performance is heterogeneous: 'built-for-purpose' instruments designed to target methane demonstrate excellent detection performance (92-100% true positive rate, 0-11% false positive rate) and quantification accuracy (slope 0.83-1.00, 44% mean absolute percentage error). Instruments repurposed for methane sensing perform more variably (detection rates 62-88%, 46% mean absolute percentage error); still, many demonstrate significant skill. Broad land scanners detect poorly at tested rates but have consistent global coverage and historical archives, motivating additional work. Artificial intelligence-based methods show promise, but caution is warranted; 79% of false positives emerge from these methods. Ground-measured cloud cover >20% degraded performance across systems, raising concerns for use in some locations. Our findings show that satellite-based measurements can achieve accurate detection and quantification of methane point sources when the source location is approximately known.

papers.abstract: Aberrant expression of neoantigenic receptor ROR1 has been identified in diverse lymphomas, including mantle cell lymphoma (MCL) and in a broad spectrum of nonlymphoid malignancies. While ROR1 has emerged as an attractive therapeutic target, its oncogenic role and the underlying mechanisms remain rather poorly characterized. Focusing on MCL, we found that ROR1 expression is heterogeneous and it can be induced under environmental stress. Inhibition of ROR1 expression resulted in cell-cycle suppression and apoptotic cell death. The ROR1 loss affected expression of numerous genes and altered phosphorylation of many proteins, including those involved in cell-cycle progression. ROR1 also promotes the synthesis of pyrimidines and purines, including induction of phosphorylation of enzymes involved in pyrimidine synthesis. Finally, we found that ROR1 induced phosphorylation of DEK and that its depletion abrogates ROR1 expression. These results provide insights into the multi-faceted oncogenic role of ROR1, further justifying targeting ROR1 in MCL and other malignancies.

papers.abstract: The objective of this study was to develop and externally validate complementary magnetic resonance imaging (MRI)-based models and their stacked combinations for preoperative World Health Organization (WHO) grading of intracranial meningioma. This retrospective multicenter study included 455 histopathologically confirmed meningiomas: a four-center development cohort (n = 346) with leave-one-center-out cross-validation and an external cohort (n = 109). Four base models used contrast-enhanced T1-weighted MRI: tumor + peritumoral radiomics, an nnU-Net segmentation-based classifier, frozen DINOv3 transfer-learning features, and clinical variables. All 15 combinations were prespecified and stacked using a linear meta-learner trained on development out-of-fold predictions. Frozen models were externally evaluated without modification. WHO 2-3 tumors comprised 24.6% overall (112/455; development 20.5%; external 37.6%). External AUCs were 0.732 for nnU-Net, 0.703 for DINOv3, 0.645 for clinical, 0.628 for radiomics. The multimodal ensemble (nnU-Net+DINOv3+Clinical) achieved the highest external AUC (0.742), exceeding radiomics (ΔAUC +0.114, p = 0.008) but not nnU-Net (ΔAUC +0.011, p = 0.737). Compared with the clinical model, discrimination was higher but nonsignificant at the prespecified threshold (ΔAUC +0.098, p = 0.050), while reclassification improved (IDI +0.109, p < 0.001). Radiomics-containing combinations performed strongly in development but lost most discrimination externally. The multimodal ensemble had an external calibration slope of 1.32 (Brier 0.190) and net benefit above default strategies at thresholds ≥ 0.23. The multimodal ensemble achieved the highest external AUC but did not significantly exceed nnU-Net, which was the most transportable single predictor of meningioma grade. Clinical variables did not improve discrimination but enabled interpretable feature-level attribution. Handcrafted radiomics lacked external transportability.

papers.abstract: The sixth Paediatric Therapeutic Development Workshop focused on desmoplastic small round cell tumours (DSRCT). Less than 20% of patients with DSRCT survive beyond 5 years and there is no targeted therapy for this disease, which represents an urgent unmet need for new therapeutics. High priority targets include the EWSR1::WT1 fusion protein, the oncogenic driver, and targeting a junction-derived neopeptide presented by HLA-A*03 and HLA-A*11 using a T-cell receptor (TCR) is a novel approach. Other targets (LRRC15, SSTR3 and SSTR5, NECTIN4, STEAP1 and mesothelin) require further validation. Targeting ERBB2/HER2 or claudin-6 by antibody-drug conjugates (ADCs) and NTRK3 by a small molecule inhibitor are promising approaches and are currently being evaluated. Existing clinical assets targeting (in order of importance) B7-H3, the DNA damage response, androgen signalling, FGFR4 and STEAP1 are also high priorities for evaluation in DSRCT, but obtaining therapeutics for clinical trials is a barrier. In view of the rarity of DSRCT, a global initiative in preclinical and clinical research to establish international trials and collect data from patients treated in a harmonised form would benefit patients. Progress can be made by a combined approach of developing new agents whilst evaluating existing therapeutics in well-designed trials.

papers.abstract: Abstract Photoacoustic imaging (PAI) as an innovative biomedical imaging modality shows high contrast and superior spatial resolution, yet remains limited by underdeveloped second near-infrared (NIR-II, 1000-1700 nm) contrast agents, particularly neglecting the NIR-IIb (1500-1700 nm) window. In this work, we designed a new class of diimmonium (DB)-based dicationic nano-agents (DB·2X, X = TFSI - , B(C 2 O 4 ) 2 - , or BF 4 - ) for 1700 nm excitation PAI. Density functional theory (DFT) calculations reveal that dicationic DB 2+ exhibits a dramatically reduced excitation energy (1.24 eV) and enhanced oscillator strength (f = 1.11) by molecular engineering, attributed to a symmetry-allowed local excitation mechanism for electronic restructuring. Single-crystal X-ray diffraction further demonstrates the intermolecular spacings >5.0 Å in DB·2X aggregates, facilitating optimized non-radiative transitions for amplified PAI signals. In vivo study using different disease models shows that DB·2TFSI nano-agents under 1700 nm excitation can achieve higher signal-to-background ratio and minimized interference from endogenous chromophores compared to conventional 1064 nm excitation. Biocompatibility assessments confirm low cytotoxicity, underscoring potential for further development of DB·2TFSI nano-agents. This work delivers a robust molecular design paradigm for non-radiative decay optimization, and for the first time establishes 1700 nm-excitable PAI nano-agents, paving the way for tissue high-quality biomedical imaging.

papers.abstract: Here we present MassNet, inspired by large-scale data corpora of text and images; MassNet is an artificial intelligence (AI)-ready data corpus for mass spectrometry (MS)-based proteomics. The corpus contains 1.5 billion tandem MS spectra from high-quality data-dependent acquisition (DDA) MS data across 35 species. Approximately 1.7 million peptide precursors are from human samples. We further present an AI-ready DDA data format called Mass Spectrometry DDA Tensor (MSDT) for compact and standardized storage, curation and reuse of data from multiple sources, which can be optionally converted to a Lightning Memory-Mapped Database for accelerated input/output in deep learning. On the basis of MassNet, we develop XuanjiNovo, a nonautoregressive transformer model that leverages a curriculum learning strategy for de novo peptide sequencing. XuanjiNovo achieves 38.35-143.57% improvement over state-of-the-art methods on human Astral data. MassNet also supports additional downstream tasks, including retention time prediction and PSM rescoring. MassNet represents a foundational MS-based proteomics data resource, marking a critical milestone for AI proteomics research.

papers.abstract: Most patients with solid tumors fail to sustain antitumor immunity, in part because immune cells cannot outcompete cancer cells inside the immunosuppressive tumor microenvironment. Here, we show the lipid-sensing transcription factor PPARδ is a compartment-specific determinant of cancer-immune fitness balance and immunotherapy efficacy. Activating PPARδ in cancer cells promotes their growth and impairs antitumor immunity, whereas activating it in immune cells drives tumor suppression and overrides tumor-promoting effects of cancer-intrinsic activation. Mechanistically, PPARδ enhances CD8+ T cell fitness against cancer through effector-associated chromatin remodeling and Cpt1a-mediated fatty acid oxidation. Therapeutically, PPARδ-activated CD8+ T cells sensitize immunotherapy-resistant microsatellite stable metastatic colorectal cancer to checkpoint blockade in mice, and pharmacological or genetic PPARδ activation enhances human chimeric antigen receptor T cell function. These findings identify compartment-specific PPARδ activity as a targetable driver of immune cell fitness that can be harnessed to improve outcomes in immunotherapy-resistant tumors.

papers.abstract: Edematous severe childhood malnutrition is distinct from the non-edematous form of malnutrition and remains a major cause of under-five mortality. Its etiology remains unclear, although aberrant one-carbon metabolism has emerged as a potential contributor. Here, we assess genetic variants at loci known to influence one-carbon metabolism, and determine their association with edematous malnutrition in Jamaica and Malawi. Six loci show evidence of association, including four related to homocysteine and folate metabolism - AHCYL1, PRICKLE2, GABBR2, and PLD2, with SNPs at the latter three also having direct effects on homocysteine-related metabolites in Mendelian Randomization. Collectively, one-carbon metabolism-related variants were significantly associated with edematous malnutrition (z = 3.2), with population differences linked to a shared East African genetic ancestry and distinct signatures of selection. These findings strengthen evidence implicating aberrant one-carbon metabolism in edematous malnutrition and highlight the utility of cell-free DNA, intra-continental admixture, and population genetics for mapping disease risk.

papers.abstract: Pyruvate dehydrogenase (PDH) complex is a key regulator of metabolism, controlling flux from glycolysis into the tricarboxylic acid (TCA) cycle. PDH is often dysregulated in metabolic diseases and cancer. We discover here that in addition to its well characterized regulation by phosphorylation, PDH activity is also regulated via inhibitory oxidation of three cysteines of the DLAT subunit - Cys488, Cys586 and Cys618. Oxidation of these cysteines increases under oxidative stress, and is highly prevalent in mouse and human tissues. This mechanism enables cells to efficiently fight oxidative stress. Under oxidative stress, cells execute a metabolic shift, blocking glycolytic flux into the TCA cycle to shunt glycolytic carbons toward the pentose phosphate pathway. This generates NADPH which cells use to detoxify H2O2 and to reduce oxidized cysteines. We find that DLAT oxidation is required for cells to mount an effective antioxidant response. Mutations preventing DLAT oxidation render PDH resistant to oxidative inhibition, impair NADPH generation, reduce peroxide detoxification, and sensitize cells to oxidative damage and death. DLAT oxidation also drives a Warburg-like metabolic phenotype of increased glucose uptake, elevated lactate secretion, and reduced TCA cycle activity. Thus DLAT oxidation is a redox-sensing mechanism that regulates PDH activity and central carbon metabolism.

papers.abstract: Solid oxide fuel cells (SOFCs) require electrolytes with high oxide-ion conductivity at low temperatures (200-400 °C) to reduce costs. Here, we report that Bi1.9Te0.1LaO4.05Br exhibits oxide-ion conductivity of 0.01 S cm⁻¹ at 233 °C within the "Norby gap" in dry atmospheres. This performance exceeds that of leading proton conductors, such as BaZr0.8Y0.2O2.9 and BaZr0.4Ce0.4Y0.1Yb0.1O2.9, as well as representative oxide-ion conductors, including yttria-stabilized zirconia (YSZ), LaGaO3-based phases (LSGM), and Bi2V0.7Sb0.3O5.5. Bi1.9Te0.1LaO4.05Br also exhibits negligible chemical expansion and high chemical stability under oxidizing, reducing, and CO2-containing atmospheres. The high conductivity is associated with a layered Sillén structure composed of Bi-containing triple fluorite-like slabs and Br layers, together with oxygen vacancies that enable vacancy-mediated oxide-ion migration. Despite the presence of excess oxide ions, oxide-ion transport predominantly occurs via a vacancy mechanism, as revealed by ab initio molecular dynamics simulations, static density functional theory calculations, and neutron diffraction analyses. These findings establish a design principle for high-performance oxide-ion conductors based on vacancy-mediated oxide-ion transport in excess-oxygen Bi-containing Sillén oxyhalides.

papers.abstract: Plastic deformation in body-centred cubic (bcc) metals and alloys is conventionally mediated by screw dislocations. Their temperature-sensitive motion is attributed to a steep rise in strength with decreasing temperature that constricts plastic zones at crack tips, leading to a ductile-to-brittle transition1. Here we evaluated the mechanical properties of group IV-V bcc refractory alloys with similar electronic structures at 20 K and found that these materials instead exhibit a plateau in tensile yield strength and fracture toughness as a function of temperature, with no apparent ductile-to-brittle transition. This behaviour arises from the global activation of twinning and an ω-phase transformation, which nucleate dislocations at interfaces before global dislocation motion. The initial mechanism is temperature insensitive and controls yielding, thereby preventing a crack-tip plastic zone from constricting with decreasing temperature.

papers.abstract: Adipose tissue has a central role in systemic energy balance and the pathogenesis of obesity and its sequelae1,2. In contrast to white adipose tissue, brown adipose tissue (BAT) uses energy to produce heat3. Detectable BAT in humans is associated with decreased prevalence of cardiometabolic diseases4. However, the complete spectrum of health conditions associated with BAT remains unknown, and high-throughput methods to quantify BAT activity in humans are lacking5,6. Here we leveraged big data and artificial intelligence to systematically define the clinical impact of BAT in a cohort of 101,243 patients from a large cancer centre. Our unbiased analyses revealed that, across all diagnoses, cardiovascular and psychiatric diseases were less prevalent in people with BAT. Using a machine learning approach, we semi-automatically quantified BAT activity in approximately 8,700 patients and demonstrated that higher BAT activity, especially in the axillary depot, is associated with lower odds of cardiometabolic diseases and healthier white fat distribution. People with BAT also exhibited more favourable glycaemic parameters, lipid profiles, inflammatory markers and echocardiographic indices. Analysis of medication usage demonstrated that angiotensin receptor blocker use was positively associated with BAT presence. As proof of concept, we showed that the angiotensin receptor blocker losartan increased brown adipocyte activity and whole-body energy expenditure. Altogether, our studies harnessing artificial intelligence and big data identify new clinical phenotypes linked to BAT and serve as a platform for drug repurposing to activate this tissue in humans.

papers.abstract: Haematopoietic stem and progenitor cell (HSPC) transplantation-mediated replacement of microglia-the reconstitution of the central nervous system microglial niche with donor-derived myeloid cells-represents a promising strategy for brain cell therapies1-7. However, the cell-intrinsic molecular regulators of HSPC-derived myeloid lineage commitment in the brain have remained largely uncharacterized. This is partially because the scarcity of primary HSPCs has rendered large-scale genetic interrogation intractable. Here we explored whether ex vivo expansion of primary cultured HSPCs (cHSPCs) enables unbiased genetic interrogation of haematopoietic differentiation. We established that cHSPCs can be genetically manipulated and readily differentiate into myeloid cells and repopulate microglia niches of the brain after transplantation. Moreover, primary neonatal astrocytes contained strong signals to induce myeloid specification of cHSPCs in vitro. To identify genes that regulate glia-induced myeloid differentiation, we successfully screened around 20,000 individual genetic perturbations and characterized genes involved in the regulation of cell signalling, cell cycle, mitochondrial function and protein translation. Among these genes was elongator acetyltransferase complex subunit 1 (Elp1), which suppressed the unfolded protein response during myeloid specification and was essential for the generation but not maintenance of myeloid cells. Our work establishes a platform to investigate the molecular mechanisms of brain myeloid biology.

papers.abstract: Decision-makers rely on weather forecasts to plant crops, manage wildfires, allocate water and energy and prepare for weather extremes1-3. Today, such forecasts enjoy unprecedented accuracy as far as 2 weeks thanks to steady advances in physics-based dynamical models and data-driven artificial intelligence models4-10. However, model skill drops precipitously at subseasonal timescales (2-6 weeks ahead) due to compounding errors, systemic model biases and the chaotic nature of the atmosphere11-15. To counter this degradation, we introduce probabilistic bias correction, a machine learning framework that substantially reduces systematic error by learning to correct historical probabilistic forecasts. When applied to the leading dynamical and artificial intelligence models from the European Centre for Medium-Range Weather Forecasts (ECMWF), probabilistic bias correction doubles the modest subseasonal skill of the AI Forecasting System16 and improves the skill of the operationally debiased dynamical model17 for 91% of pressure, 92% of temperature and 98% of precipitation targets. We designed probabilistic bias correction for operational deployment, and, in the 2025 real-time forecasting competition of ECMWF18, its global forecasts were the best for all weather variables and lead times, outperforming the dynamical models from six operational forecasting centres, an international dynamical multimodel ensemble, the AI Forecasting System of ECMWF and the forecasting systems of 34 teams worldwide. These probabilistic skill gains translate into more accurate prediction of extreme events and have the potential to improve agricultural planning, energy management and disaster preparedness in vulnerable communities19.

papers.abstract: The epidermis is a stratified epithelium comprising proliferative basal cells and differentiated suprabasal cells that are continuously renewed throughout life. Conflicting theories have been proposed regarding the heterogeneity of the basal cell layer, with some studies proposing that all proliferative cells have self-renewal potential during homeostasis1-5. Meanwhile, others posit a model in which stem cell differentiation occurs through an intermediate transit-amplifying-like progenitor state with strictly limited proliferative potential6-10. Here, to determine the heterogeneity and pattern of cell fate, we performed intravital time-lapse imaging to track the fate of lineage-labelled cells in the skin interfollicular epidermis. Results from quantitative analyses of clonal dynamics support a two-compartment model of epidermal homeostasis, whereby basal cells are organized in a stem cell-transit-amplifying cell hierarchy. Critical to these conclusions was the discovery of sexual dimorphism in epidermal fate, with female mice showing a highly synchronized pattern of cell division, differentiation and delamination that contributes to accelerated wound healing. Single-cell RNA sequencing, transcriptional profiling and clonal analyses of castrated mice revealed that male sex hormones promote stem cell differentiation and delamination. In summary, our study provides insight into the functional identity of the stem cell population and identifies sex-specific differences in the regulation of epidermal stem cells and transit-amplifying cell fate.

papers.abstract: Neuronal microexons are a highly conserved class of alternative splicing events enriched in genes with critical functions in nervous system biology1,2. Microexon splicing is often disrupted in the brains of autistic individuals, and mice with microexon deficiencies display autism-like phenotypes1,3,4. However, the full landscape of microexons is not known, and the impact of genetic variation on these exons has not been systematically investigated. Here, through extensive transcriptome profiling, we detect hundreds of new microexons, including many with neuronal subtype-specific splicing patterns, and others that activate nonsense-mediated mRNA decay. Using machine learning, we define a sequence code predictive of neuronally spliced microexons and use this to identify critical regulatory elements surrounding the expanded microexon repertoire. This code further reveals genomic variants predicted to alter microexon splicing in individuals affected by autism, with rare variants having the strongest estimated impact. These variants are mostly detected in idiopathic individuals and are associated with autism status. They also converge on synaptic and other autism-linked genes, as well as genes not previously linked to autism. Our results collectively define an expanded repertoire of microexons, delineate their regulatory code, and pinpoint variants predicted to affect their splicing, with implications for the disruption of functions central to neuronal biology and brain disorders.

papers.abstract: Social networks shape behaviour, affect information dissemination and undergird collective action. And they can be exploited in the design of interventions in these domains1-7. Although social networks obey fundamental principles, such as the degree distribution8,9, they can nevertheless evolve as ties form and break. Here, through a randomized controlled trial involving a total of 8,331 people in 110 remote Honduran villages, we evaluate the secondary effects of a 22-month public-health intervention1 on pre-existing social-network structure. We used a design in which a varying fraction of village households received the intervention, and villages in which no one received the intervention were used as the primary reference group. In 'low-dosage' villages (in which 5-30% of households received the intervention), people who received the intervention tended to sever ties with untreated individuals to whom they previously went for health advice. Conversely, in high-dosage villages (50-100%), treated individuals increased their ties. These average changes are explained mainly by tie dynamics; that is, treated-treated pairs persist and form new links, whereas treated-untreated ties dissolve. A mediation analysis indicates that absorption of health information increases the likelihood of tie formation and persistence. The rewiring patterns generally lasted for three years after the intervention ceased. Moreover, although the intervention delivered health information, it reshaped friendship and financial ties, not just health-advice connections. In aggregate, the introduction of a new information regime acted as a kind of social institution, rewiring individuals' connections even though the overall degree distribution of village-wide networks remained relatively stable.

papers.abstract: Plastics have become an integral part of our modern society, largely because they are generally regarded as chemically inert under normal circumstances. However, plastics fragmented into microplastics (less than 5 mm in size) have recently raised significant public concerns, and have been detected widely across ecosystems and human tissues with increasing environmental and health risks1-5. Here we show that commodity microplastics exhibit intrinsic physicochemical activity in water, manifested by the spontaneous generation of reactive oxygen species that increases with interfacial hydrophobicity and strongly correlates with interfacial electrostatics. Ab initio calculations support these observations and reveal that hydroxide oxidation becomes energetically more favourable at increasingly hydrophobic microplastic-water interfaces through the combined effects of partial solvation and electrostatics. These interfacial properties and the resulting oxidative chemistry have direct implications for biomolecular adsorption, protein aggregation, and even cellular damage. Together, our findings challenge the prevailing paradigm of plastic inertness, identify a possibly overlooked mechanism for the detrimental effects of microplastics on health and the environment, and contribute to a fundamental understanding of the structure-activity relationship of interfacial water, which may inform the design of safer and more sustainable plastic materials.

papers.abstract: Pain during propofol injection is common, yet little is known about how often patients remember this experience after anesthesia or which perioperative factors influence memory formation during induction. In this prospective single-center observational cohort study, English-speaking adults (≥ 18 years) receiving propofol under general anesthesia (GA) or monitored anesthesia care (MAC) were enrolled. Perioperative characteristics, intravenous access details, anesthetic medications and clinician-observed injection pain were recorded. On postoperative day 1, patients were interviewed using a standardized questionnaire assessing recall of discomfort during induction. Univariate and multivariate logistic regression analyses calculated adjusted odds ratios (aOR) and identified factors associated with recall. Of the 1,699 enrolled patients, 1,319 completed the postoperative day 1 assessment; 8.1% reported recall of injection discomfort. Multivariate analysis indicated that younger age (aOR = 1.03; 95% CI = 1.01-1.04; p < 0.001), female gender (aOR = 1.69; 95% CI = 1.02-2.82; p = 0.044), hand IV placement (aOR = 2.164; CI 95% = 1.287-3.636; p = 0.004), and absence of midazolam premedication (aOR = 2.62; 95% CI = 1.44-4.78; p = 0.002) were associated with increased recall. Approximately one in twelve patients recalled discomfort during propofol injection. Patient characteristics and modifiable anesthetic practices, particularly premedication and intravenous access site, were associated with memory of propofol injection discomfort. These findings highlight that memory formation during induction represents a distinct and clinically relevant patient-centered outcome.

papers.abstract: Anxiety disorders affect more than one-quarter of the global population, but current first-line therapies suffer from slow onset and limited efficacy, highlighting the urgent need for novel pathogenic targets. Psychological stress disrupts iron homeostasis in the brain and alters neural circuit excitability; however, the mechanism underlying these two processes remains elusive. Here, we identify a cell type-specific iron signaling pathway between neurons and astrocytes that mediates stress-induced anxiety by regulating synaptic iron transport in the ventral hippocampal-medial prefrontal cortex circuit. In a chronic restraint stress model in male mice, stress induces activity-dependent HMGB1 expression and release from medial prefrontal cortex pyramidal neurons, which bind to astrocytic TLR4 to stimulate local hepcidin secretion. Hepcidin degrades ferroportin at ventral hippocampal-medial prefrontal cortex axonal terminals in a retrograde manner, blocking presynaptic iron efflux. The resultant iron accumulation in ventral hippocampal-medial prefrontal cortex projection neurons increases their intrinsic excitability via a ferroplasticity mechanism and anxiety-like behaviors. Notably, intranasal administration of HMGB1/TLR4 antagonists efficiently restored synaptic iron flux and alleviated anxiety in both stress-induced and innate high-anxiety models. Collectively, our findings define a retrograde ferrosynaptic neuroglial coupling mechanism through which stress induces anxiety independently of classical synaptic transmission. This work establishes the HMGB1-TLR4-hepcidin-FPN axis as a druggable therapeutic target and provides a conceptual framework for understanding how iron metabolism operates as a transcellular social coordination system in emotional regulation.

papers.abstract: Humoral immunity, a fundamental branch of adaptive immunity, relies on B lymphocytes and the antibodies they produce to eliminate extracellular pathogens and neutralize toxins. The development, activation, and differentiation of B cells are tightly regulated by epigenetic mechanisms-including DNA methylation, histone modifications, chromatin dynamics, RNA modifications, and noncoding RNAs-that modulate gene expression without altering the DNA sequence, orchestrating key events such as V(D)J recombination, class switch recombination, somatic hypermutation, germinal center reactions, and the generation of memory B cells and plasma cells. In this review, we summarize how these five categories of epigenetic regulators-together with their respective writers, erasers, readers, and effectors-including DNMT3A/3B and TET enzymes, histone-modifying enzymes, SWI/SNF and INO80 remodeling complexes, N6-methyladenosine and 5-methylcytosine machineries, and microRNAs and long noncoding RNAs-collectively govern B-cell fate decisions, from early lineage commitment in the bone marrow, through germinal center dynamics, to terminal differentiation into plasma cells or memory B cells. We further examine how aberrant epigenetic programs in B cells contribute to pathogenesis across four major disease categories: B-cell malignancies, metabolic and cardiovascular diseases, autoimmune disorders, and infectious diseases. We also discuss sex-biased epigenetic mechanisms, particularly escape from X-chromosome inactivation, that may underlie the female predominance of autoimmune diseases. Finally, we discuss the therapeutic implications of targeting epigenetic regulators and assess the potential of epigenetic signatures as biomarkers.

papers.abstract: Combining inhibition of poly(ADP-ribose) polymerase and androgen receptor (AR) pathway has demonstrated clinical activity in men with metastatic prostate cancer, although the extent of benefit in tumors lacking homologous recombination repair (HRR) gene alterations remains uncertain. We conducted a randomized phase 2 trial evaluating talazoparib plus enzalutamide versus enzalutamide alone in men with high-volume metastatic hormone-naive prostate cancer (mHNPC). Fifty-four patients starting androgen deprivation therapy received two cycles of enzalutamide lead-in before 1:2 randomization to enzalutamide (n = 17) or enzalutamide plus talazoparib (n = 37). The primary endpoint was met, with a 73% prostate-specific antigen (PSA) <0.2 ng ml-1 response rate at 12 months in the combination arm (95% confidence interval (CI) = 56-86%), exceeding the prespecified efficacy threshold (P < 0.001); the PSA <0.2 rate in the control arm was 64.7% (95% CI = 38-86%, P = 0.54 for exploratory comparison between arms). Grade ≥3 adverse events occurred in 68% patients receiving the combination versus 35% with enzalutamide alone, predominantly anemia (41%). Two fatal therapy-emergent myeloid neoplasms occurred in the enzalutamide plus talazoparib arm in patients with underlying genomic susceptibility. Analyses of paired tumor biopsies acquired at baseline and during enzalutamide lead-in phase demonstrated marked tumor transcriptional reprogramming after AR inhibition, including suppression of proliferation-associated and HRR-related gene expression programs, but without functional impairment of homologous recombination activity. Overall, talazoparib plus enzalutamide demonstrated clinical activity in patients with high-volume mHNPC but did not establish clear additional clinical benefit over enzalutamide alone in this biomarker-unselected population, while being associated with increased toxicity. papers.abstract: A major barrier to cancer therapy is the emergence of drug-tolerant states that allow tumor cells to bypass the targeted pathway. These refractory states arise through reversible cellular plasticity, a process that also occurs during development and regeneration, giving rise to new lineages or phenotypes and restoring drug sensitivity upon treatment withdrawal. Over time, genetic mutations may accumulate, leading to permanent resistance. This paradigm expands the focus from targeting genetic mechanisms alone to also exploiting nongenetic vulnerabilities, driving clinical strategies that prevent or eliminate plastic and transformed populations. Here, we provide an overview of nongenetic plasticity mechanisms and their emerging clinical applications.

papers.abstract: Personalized neoantigen-targeting cancer vaccines in the adjuvant setting are of increasing interest across malignancies. Here we report the results of a phase 1 clinical trial testing the feasibility and safety of personalized neoantigen-targeting cancer vaccines for high-grade epithelial ovarian cancer. 'NeoVax' consisted of pools of synthetic long peptides targeting patient-specific neoantigens admixed with the immunostimulant poly-ICLC, was combined with delayed administration of anti-PD-1 antibody, and was tested in ten patients (one newly diagnosed patient (Cohort A) and nine patients at first recurrence (Cohort B)) with platinum-sensitive ovarian cancer following standard-of-care platinum doublet chemotherapy. Nine of 12 evaluable Cohort B patients were vaccinated (75%, 90% CI 47-93%) and 1 of 9 Cohort A patients (11%, 90% CI 0.6-43%). No unexpected safety signals were encountered and no patients discontinued treatment due to toxicity. Across patients, >70% selected targets remained detectable by noninvasive cell-free DNA analysis despite a median of 6.5 months from the time of diagnostic biopsy to vaccine administration, during which, patients received standard-of-care chemotherapy. Biomarker analysis was suggestive of biologic activity of the vaccine in six of ten patients and this was associated with broader tumor and vaccine-specific immune responses in blood and tumor following vaccination. Resistant tumor clones reflected diverse mechanisms affecting antigen presentation, indicative of immune-selective pressure exerted by vaccination. Overall, the interplay between the repertoire of antigens presented by the tumor and the breadth of induced immunity seemed to dictate clinical efficacy following vaccination. papers.abstract: Human urine represents a nutrient-rich reservoir that, if recycled, could significantly offset global fertilizer demands. Yet, its potential remains largely underexploited because rapid urea hydrolysis at the source drives N and P losses via uncontrolled precipitation, while causing pipe clogging and malodor formation. Here, we report a wollastonite (CaSiO3)-integrated electrochemical alkalization and oxidation (EAO) system that enables concurrent urea stabilization and phosphorus recovery. Anodic proton-driven dissolution of CaSiO3 releases Ca2+, which combines with cathodically generated alkalinity to promote phosphate precipitation, whereas anodic oxidation suppresses urease-mediated urea hydrolysis. We show that the driving force lies in the microenvironment near the electrode, which has distinct pH, Ca2+ and active‑chlorine gradients. Treating two‑fold diluted urine at 12 A m-2 yields the most energy‑efficient scenario (20.11 kWh kg-1 P, 2.99 kWh m-3 urine), achieving 96.0% phosphate recovery and robust urea stabilization in real urine. We expect the EAO system to create a scalable electrochemical route to close nutrient loops in decentralized sanitation, supporting sustainable fertilizer production and urine management.

papers.abstract: This study reports a series of CRBN molecular glues that selectively induce proteasomal degradation of VAV1, a hematopoietic-specific signaling protein and key target in hematological malignancies and autoimmune diseases. Using unbiased global proteomics, we identify phenyl-glutarimide derivatives (e.g., NGT-201-12) as effective VAV1 degraders that engage its C-terminal SH3 domain (SH3-2). We elucidate a non-canonical RT-loop degron (RDxS motif, residues 796-799) in SH3-2, distinct from previously characterized G-loop degrons, supported by the physics- and AI-driven GluePlex workflow and site-directed mutagenesis. Applying Free Energy Perturbation (FEP) to predicted ternary structures yields cooperativity metrics that correlate with degradation potency, overcoming limitations of standard docking and enabling prospective ranking of analogs-even from weak initial binders. We further show that conformational restriction via halogen substitution (e.g., NGT-201-18) potentiates degradation, a principle rationalized by DFT calculations, while comprehensive SAR studies chart a roadmap for next-generation degraders. Dose-response proteomics confirms VAV1 as the primary target and reveals LIMD1, bearing a canonical G-loop, as an off-target, showing that one glue can engage disparate degrons. These findings expand the landscape of CRBN neosubstrate recognition and offer a therapeutic strategy for targeting VAV1.

papers.abstract: The plant hormone jasmonoyl-isoleucine (JA-Ile) reallocates resources from growth towards induced defenses upon microbial or herbivore attacks or other environmental threats. JA-Ile and its precursor jasmonic acid (JA) undergo complex enzymatic turnover that shape hormonal dynamics for optimal signaling. JA-Ile is inactivated through gradual oxidation by CYP94 monooxygenases, followed by 12-OH-JA-Ile deconjugation towards 12-OH-JA. 12-OH-JA was believed to originate also from direct JA hydroxylation by JAO/JOX dioxygenases. Here we investigate the nature and origins of hydroxy-JAs and their derivatives upon stress responses in Arabidopsis. Using a set of analytical methods to explore enzyme assays and multiple pathway-impaired mutants, we show that JAO enzymes produce exclusively 11-OH-JA rather than 12-OH-JA and define a separate branch in JA catabolism. Upon leaf wounding, the CYP94/AH and, to a lesser extent, the JAO pathways direct the respective accumulation of 12- and 11-OH-JAs and their 11/12-glucosylated and 12-sulfated derivatives with isoform-specific occurrences. In contrast, Botrytis infection triggers the exclusive accumulation of 11-OH-JA and 11-Glc-O-JA with complex patterns of HSO4-JA. Finally, treatment of jar1 seedlings with 11-OH-JA does not trigger transcriptional changes, reinforcing the notion that the JAO/11-OH-JA pathway represents a metabolic sink modulating JA-Ile formation. Our findings elucidate the 11-OH-JA biosynthetic pathway and highlight stress-specific hydroxylation signatures.

papers.abstract: Wireless body sensor networks could enable unencumbered human-machine interfaces for robotics, assistive healthcare, and immersive computing. However, their widespread adoption remains constrained by bulky batteries and inefficient wireless communication. Here, we report a battery-free wireless body sensor network enabled by a dual-mode metamaterial textile for continuous and unobtrusive human-machine interactions. The textile, digitally embroidered with liquid-metal fibers, establishes ultra-wideband electromagnetic pathways to simultaneously support efficient near-field power transfer and Bluetooth communication across the entire human body. This architecture enhances data throughput by 37.8 times and doubles wireless power transfer efficiency compared with emerging near-field clothing. When worn, the metamaterial-integrated clothing allows an NFC-enabled smartphone to serve as a central hub, wirelessly delivering power to and acquiring multimodal signals from distributed battery-free HMI sensors. We demonstrate that this battery-free body sensor network remains robust during motion and enables intuitive, unencumbered interactions in robotic control, virtual reality, and human digital twins.

papers.abstract: Polyploidy, the possession of more than two sets of chromosomes in somatic cells, is a major driver in the diversification of flowering plants. Whereas an association between the occurrence of polyploids and latitude suggests a major impact of temperature on their global distribution, it remains unknown how polyploid frequency varies at regional spatial scales, leaving unclear the overall robustness of such relationship and its major determinants. Here, we present a flora-wide dataset of newly sampled, georeferenced ploidy occurrence data for ca. 42,000 samples of angiosperms collected along 101 elevational transects across the Eastern European Alps. Based on these data, we find that on a regional level polyploid frequency decreases with elevation, in contrast to expectations derived from global latitudinal distribution patterns. Moreover, polyploid frequency increases with distance from glacial refugia for samples below the timberline, particularly for plants with limited dispersal abilities. These results suggest that range dynamics associated with Pleistocene climatic fluctuations rather than current temperature may have played a predominant role for the current distribution of polyploids in temperate mountain ranges. In sum, our systematic fine-scale survey identified a complex interplay between historical processes and current environments on polyploid distribution that have remained undetected at the global scale.

papers.abstract: Through cumulative cultural evolution, human populations discover novel solutions that allow them to solve complex problems. However, populations also reliably develop and sustain practices that are costly yet appear to have no effect on their stated outcome, such as bloodletting, divination, and malicious sorcery. Here, we show that ineffective, costly solutions can develop and be maintained because of their cognitive appeal. In a pre-registered transmission-chain experiment, participants were tasked with developing a solution to a problem over several trials, after which they passed instructions onto the subsequent generation. The visual appearance of the experimental task was manipulated to vary the extent to which cognitive biases could interfere with participants' expectations of efficacy, enabling a direct test of the effect of cognitive appeal on cumulative cultural evolution. Participants in the low-appeal treatment (n = 240) progressively develop more efficient solutions across generations. Participants in the high-appeal treatment (n = 240), in contrast, produce costlier solutions, and we did not observe a statistically significant increase in efficiency over the course of the experiment. These results suggest that, even under conditions favorable to cumulative cultural evolution, a form of cognitive appeal can alone prevent the process and promote the emergence and cultural persistence of ineffective solutions.

papers.abstract: Two-dimensional (2D) metal oxides (MOs) are crucial materials in semiconductor optoelectronics and energy applications. Recently, ultra-confined and anisotropic polaritons, which are hybrid light-matter waves, in 2D MOs have renewed interest in the field of nanophotonics. With natural abundance, diverse compositions, and rich symmetries, MOs exhibit a wide range of electromagnetic responses from the visible to terahertz spectral range, providing various polariton platforms for designing on-chip photonic integrated circuits. In this Review, we discuss crystal symmetry and polaritons in MOs, present intrinsic and extrinsic manipulation approaches, and summarize strategies for synthesizing 2D polaritonic MOs. We also propose 2D MO-based polaritonic device architectures for use in heat management, photonics, and biosensing, all of which could be integrated into future photonic chips. Overall, with the rapid flourishing of 2D MO polaritonics, this review aims to stimulate further exploration and innovation for next-generation on-chip photonic systems.

papers.abstract: Despite dramatic human-driven changes across ecosystems, local-scale aggregate biodiversity metrics are often surprisingly stable, even as communities experience substantial reorganization of species identities and relative abundances. While rare species are often thought to be more vulnerable to these changes, emerging evidence suggests that common species may experience disproportionately greater declines. To evaluate these alternatives, we synthesize population trends for species initially rare or common across assemblages from 4748 sites within 129 studies spanning terrestrial, freshwater, and marine ecosystems. We quantify how population trends relate to initial abundances using hierarchical Bayesian models that account for regression to the mean and include realm, taxon, and environmental covariates. We find consistently stronger declines among formerly common species in marine and terrestrial assemblages, while freshwater assemblages show no clear directional pattern. Rare species present at the start also decline, but less so than common species, while colonists that were not present at the start of the time series compensate for losses within the rarest abundance category. Climate change and anthropogenic drivers modulate these trends, with increasing temperature and non-climatic human pressures attenuating losses of initially common species, particularly in marine systems. Overall, we find widespread declines in common species through time, with potential functional consequences.

papers.abstract: Palladium plays a three-fold role in modern science and technology: it serves as a key active center in modern catalytic synthetic methods, occurs as unwanted trace contamination that influences new catalysts development and can lead to false-positive reports, and is an emerging environmental pollutant from automotive catalysts. High activity at ppm/ppb loadings and the necessity to analyze sub-micromolar concentrations of samples are common challenges in these applications, making reliable Pd identification essential. Mass spectrometry (MS) can detect Pd-containing ions in complex mixtures, but post-spectral recognition is difficult when minor Pd signals overlap with signals from other components and fine isotope structures are not visible. The present study introduces a machine-learning-based (ML) approach featuring a graph algorithm for the separation of signals from different multicharged ions and deep-learning classifiers for the automatic recognition of Pd ions in mass spectra of multi-component mixtures down to 10-8 mol L-1. It is applied to Pd intermediates in catalytic synthesis, contaminant catalysis and environmental samples. The scalability of the approach enables extension to Ni, Cu, Ag, Cl and Br. With the developed ML/MS workflow, Pd and other important elements could be automatically revealed; thus, routine MS hardware could be transformed into high-performance scanners.

papers.abstract: Conventional waveguide optical resonators face inherent limitations of low damage thresholds, limited coupling tunability, and stochastic resonance. To overcome these, we introduce a geometrical-optics resonator (GOR) framework, emulating free-space reflection and thin-film coupling on-chip. Using ultra-wide waveguides with total internal reflection (TIR) mirrors and frustrated-TIR couplers, GORs eliminate conventional constraints. Fabricated devices achieve intrinsic Q-factors >1 million and enable tunable microwave photonic filters operating distortion-free at about 10× higher optical power. Design flexibility allows precisely tuned coupled resonators, facilitating cascaded networks for spectral engineering. Demonstrated GOR photonic molecules exhibit dynamically adjustable mode splitting (0.49 free spectral range), nearing theoretical limits. The platform also realizes record-large-scale Floquet topological photonic insulators with 1281 GOR lattices, supporting robust edge modes against defects and a broadband continuum. The GOR sets new performance benchmarks, enabling scalable platforms for quantum simulation and topological networks while driving integrated photonics toward higher density and system-level integration.

papers.abstract: Metal halide perovskite quantum dots (QDs) are promising materials for developing low-cost and high-performance quantum dot-based light-emitting diodes (QLEDs). Despite external quantum efficiency (EQE) comparable to II-VI/III-V QLEDs, perovskite QD counterparts achieve peak EQE at low luminance/current density and exhibit significantly more pronounced efficiency roll-off, owing primarily to their ionic character and soft lattice. Engineering a robust surface is essential to ensure the structural stability of perovskite QDs, yet achieving this remains a critical challenge. Here, we develop an H2S-mediated surface passivation strategy. Experimental measurements confirm Pb-S coordination and a reduction in oleylamine ligand density, while DFT calculations suggest that (H2S)2 dimers may additionally interact with Cs-vacancy-related surface environments. This H2S-induced surface reconstruction creates a more robust surface coordination environment in CsPbI3 QDs. Benefiting from the enhanced surface stability, LEDs incorporating the treated CsPbI3 QDs possess increased ion migration barrier, balanced charge injection, and suppressed Auger recombination. These combined improvements yield a peak EQE of 30.71% at 52 mA cm-2 and 91.46 W Sr-1 m-2, with the device maintaining EQEs of 18.59% at ~500 mA cm-2 and 21.15% at ~500 W Sr-1 m-2, as well as an operational half-lifetime of 104,587 h.

papers.abstract: Spatiotemporal transcriptomics (STT) integrates spatially resolved gene expression with temporal information derived from staged samples, paired treatment specimens, or computational inference, providing a framework for reconstructing tissue-level dynamics. In the tumour microenvironment (TME), STT extends static molecular and cellular maps by revealing how cellular neighbourhoods and functional niches are reorganised during tumour evolution. This review examines how STT characterises TME remodelling during malignant transformation, invasion, metastasis, ageing, and treatment response. We discuss strategies for resolving temporal dynamics, including stage-stratified sampling, paired or serial specimens, pseudotime and trajectory inference, and complementary intravital imaging. We further consider how spatiotemporal analyses can connect changes in cellular states, spatial organisation, and intercellular interactions with clinically relevant tumour phenotypes. By linking the spatial organisation of the TME with stage- and treatment-associated molecular changes, STT may improve the prioritisation of candidate targets, treatment stratification, and the development of precision oncology strategies.

papers.abstract: The objective of this study was to verify that a strategy involving prophylactic exposure of the inferior parathyroid glands and preservation of their venous blood flow-achieved through early identification and protection of their venous drainage-can enhance the success rate of maintaining glandular perfusion and effectively reduce the incidence of postoperative hypoparathyroidism. This study included 600 patients who underwent total thyroidectomy with concomitant bilateral central neck dissection between November 2019 and December 2025. Patients were divided into two groups based on the surgical technique: Group A (n = 244), in which a prophylactic approach was used to protect the venous drainage of the inferior parathyroid glands, and Group B (n = 356), which underwent conventional in situ preservation of the inferior parathyroid glands. A comparison was made between the two groups regarding both the percentage of inferior parathyroid glands successfully preserved in situ and the incidence of postoperative hypoparathyroidism. The rate of visualization of inferior parathyroid glands with optimal blood supply was significantly higher in Group A than in Group B (p < 0.001). Postoperation parathyroid hormone level in Group A was significantly higher than that in Group B (25.15 [19.39, 33.58] pg/mL vs. 19.12 [9.82, 28.85] pg/mL, p < 0.001). In Group A, the rates of postoperative hypoparathyroidism-encompassing both transient and permanent forms-were significantly lower than those in Group B (p < 0.001). The method of prophylactically exposing the inferior parathyroid glands and preserving their venous system-termed prophylactic preservation of inferior parathyroid venous blood flow-is achieved through early identification and protection of their venous drainage. This approach enhances the success rate of maintaining glandular blood supply and effectively reduces the incidence of postoperative hypoparathyroidism.

papers.abstract: Prostate cancer (PCa) mortality disparities are partly driven by unequal access to care. Transportation barriers may limit access to definitive treatment. We studied how driving travel time affects receipt of definitive PCa treatment. We conducted a cohort study of men with non-metastatic PCa (2000-2015; follow-up through 2018) across the metropolitan area cancer registries of seven US states. Travel time was estimated using Google Maps isochrones representing driving time thresholds to reach the hospital appended to geomasked residential addresses. Outcomes were "no treatment," "radical surgery," or "radiotherapy". Covariate-adjusted multinomial logistic regression with interaction terms assessed modification by sociodemographic factors. The study included 132,939 men, of whom 37.0% received no treatment, 41.0% underwent surgery, and 22.0% received radiotherapy. Longer driving time (≥ 90 min vs. < 30 min) was associated with higher radical prostatectomy (aOR: 1.08, 95% CI: 1.03, 1.12), but lower radiotherapy (0.72, 95% CI: 0.69-0.76). Subgroup analyses revealed higher surgery associated with longer driving times among those in nSES Q1 (aOR: 1.33, 95% CI: 1.21-1.45) vs. Q5 (aOR: 0.94, 95% CI: 0.86-1.04), those in low (aOR: 1.16, 95% CI: 1.09-1.24) vs. high (aOR: 1.03, 95% CI: 0.98-1.09) population density areas, and those with regional (aOR: 1.30, 95% CI: 1.14-1.48) vs. localized (aOR: 1.05, 95% CI: 1.00-1.09) disease. Longer driving time was mostly associated with lower odds of radiotherapy across sociodemographic subgroups. Higher travel time was associated with lower radiotherapy receipt, but higher surgery use in deprived and rural patients, warranting further investigation.

papers.abstract: Venetoclax (VEN)-based regimens improve remission in acute myeloid leukemia (AML), but infectious toxicity remains a concern. We compared infection profiles under VEN-based versus conventional therapy in newly diagnosed, non-M3 AML at a single tertiary center (2015-2024; n = 358; VEN = 156; non-VEN = 202). After 1:1 propensity-score matching on nine baseline covariates (115 per group), we assessed infection rates and event density (events per 1000 person-days) by site and pathogen, time to first infection (120-day cumulative incidence), and landmark associations between early infections and progression-free survival (PFS). Baseline predictors of microbiologically documented infection (MDI) were modeled in the pre-matching cohort. VEN was associated with higher febrile-neutropenia (FN) event density (IRR, 1.77; 95% CI, 1.33-2.36; p < 0.001; 16.40 vs. 9.27 per 1000 person-days). Site-level patterns diverged: upper-respiratory and lung infections showed lower first-event incidence with VEN, whereas skin/soft-tissue and perianal sites showed higher event density without higher patient-level incidence. By pathogen, bacterial and fungal first events were fewer with VEN while event densities were comparable; viral infections occurred earlier and accrued higher cumulative incidence. Cumulatively, the first infection was lower with VEN at days 30, 60, and 90 but converged by day 120. In the pre-matching cohort, higher HCT-CI (1-2/≥ 3 vs. 0) and higher DBIL independently predicted MDI, while female sex predicted lower risk. MDIs within 90 days-bacterial/fungal-driven-were associated with inferior PFS at 100 and 365 days, whereas early viral infections showed no association.

papers.abstract: Household size and composition may be associated with health-related quality of life (HRQoL), yet these associations remain poorly characterized among cancer survivors. We examined how household adult composition and presence of children were associated with HRQoL among U.S. cancer survivors. Adult (aged ≥ 18 years) cancer survivors were included from the Behavioral Risk Factor Surveillance System (BRFSS) 2017-2024. Household composition was defined by number of adults (1, 2, or ≥ 3) and presence of children (none vs. ≥ 1). Outcomes included poor physical health (PPH), poor mental health (PMH; each defined as ≥ 14 days/month), and fair/poor general health. Multivariable Poisson regression was used to estimate adjusted prevalence ratios (aPRs) with 95% confidence intervals. Among 138,360 cancer survivors, 45.2% (n = 62,605) resided in single-adult households, 47.1% (n = 65,132) in two-adult households, and 7.7% (n = 10,623) in households with ≥ 3 adults; children were present in 5.1% (n = 7063) of households. After adjustment, two-adult household residence was associated with lower prevalence of poor physical health (adjusted prevalence ratio [aPR] 0.93, 95% CI 0.87-0.99), poor mental health (aPR 0.90, 95% CI 0.82-0.98), and fair/poor general health (aPR 0.92, 95% CI 0.88-0.97; all p ≤ 0.019) compared with single-adult households. Residence with ≥ 3 adults and child presence was not associated with any examined HRQoL outcome after adjustment. Exploratory stratified analyses identified associations within several sociodemographic subgroups. Two-adult household residence was consistently associated with better HRQoL. Single-adult household status may represent a simple social risk marker to inform survivorship assessment.

papers.abstract: Triple-negative breast cancers (TNBCs) are associated with poor prognosis and chemoresistance. Recent reports indicate that extracellular matrix (ECM) molecules, such as integrins, could influence TNBC development. Integrins are adhesion macromolecules that modulate ECM characteristics such as stiffening of ECM and being associated with hypoxia. Therefore, dysregulation in integrins could compromise the efficient delivery of cancer treatments. Some peptides and aptamers can directly target integrins, and they are now being studied; however, most monoclonal antibodies and PARP inhibitors that are used for TNBC do not directly target integrins. Integrins and the ECM can change the way these treatments work. Currently, the efficacy of these candidates is still being evaluated, and the majority of studies are in the early phase of development. The present article reviews the role of integrins in cancer development and captures the state-of-the-art evidence on the therapeutic targeting of integrins in breast cancer. Also, solutions to overcome challenges in the field are suggested.

papers.abstract: This study aimed to explore the correlation between the ability of M2-type tumor-correlated macrophage-derived exosomes (EXOs) to trigger the aggressiveness of gastric cancer (GC) cells and the miR-132-3p expression. EXOs were isolated from the conditioned media of M0 and M2 macrophages and characterized by transmission electron microscopy and Western blotting. miR-132-3p expression was determined by qRT-PCR. HGC-27 cells were divided into the control, miR-132-3p mimic, miR-132-3p inhibitor, M0-EXO, and M2-EXO groups. Cell viability, proliferation, migration, and invasion were assessed using CCK-8, EdU, and Transwell assays. Intracellular GSH, SOD, MDA, and iron levels were measured using colorimetric assays. FTH1, LIFR, and GPX4 expressions were detected by Western blotting. RNA sequencing and bioinformatics analyses were performed to investigate miR-132-3p-mediated transcriptional changes and ferroptosis-related pathways in HGC-27 cells. miR-132-3p was significantly enriched in M2 macrophage-derived exosomes and was highly expressed in GC, with its expression associated with tumor stage, grade, and other clinicopathological features. M2-Exo treatment significantly increased miR-132-3p levels in HGC-27 cells. Both miR-132-3p overexpression and M2-Exo treatment enhanced the proliferation, migration, and invasion of HGC-27 cells, and were accompanied by reduced intracellular iron and MDA levels, increased GSH content and SOD activity, upregulated FTH1 and GPX4 expression, and decreased LIFR expression. In contrast, miR-132-3p inhibition produced largely opposite effects. RNA-seq identified 275 differentially expressed genes following miR-132-3p overexpression, including 216 upregulated and 59 downregulated genes. GO and KEGG analyses revealed significant alterations in biological processes and pathways related to oxygen transport, ATP synthesis, oxidative phosphorylation, thermogenesis, spliceosome function, and endoplasmic reticulum protein processing. Integration of the RNA-seq-derived DEGs with FerrDb identified 12 ferroptosis-related DEGs, including 11 upregulated genes and 1 downregulated gene. qRT-PCR validation showed expression patterns broadly consistent with the RNA-seq results. miR-132-3p expression in the EXOs of M2-type macrophages was significantly elevated, and the EXOs of M2-type macrophages significantly triggered the aggressiveness of GC cells and inhibited ferroptosis in GC cells, which may be resulting from the prevention of ferroptosis through the transport of miR-132-3p; nevertheless, the specific mechanism of action needs to be further elucidated.
