papers.abstract: Colorectal cancer (CRC) remains a major global health burden. Chemotherapy is central to the management of advanced or metastatic disease and is also used in perioperative settings, but outcomes vary substantially. The neutrophil-to-lymphocyte ratio (NLR) is an inexpensive and readily available marker of systemic inflammation; its prognostic association in chemotherapy-treated CRC warrants focused evaluation. This study adhered to PRISMA guidelines and was registered with PROSPERO. PubMed, Embase, Web of Science, and the Cochrane Library were searched from inception to July 15, 2025. Studies evaluating pretreatment NLR in relation to overall survival (OS) or a secondary progression- or recurrence-related time-to-event outcome, including progression-free survival (PFS), disease-free survival (DFS), or recurrence-free survival (RFS), in chemotherapy-treated CRC patients were eligible. Study screening, data extraction, and quality assessment were independently conducted by two reviewers. Pooled hazard ratios (HRs) and 95% confidence intervals (CIs) were calculated using random-effects models. Subgroup and leave-one-out sensitivity analyses were performed. Thirty-eight studies (41 cohorts; 11,346 patients) were included. Elevated pretreatment NLR was associated with poorer OS (HR = 1.68, 95% CI 1.54-1.84; P < 0.0001) and poorer progression- or recurrence-related survival (HR = 1.61, 95% CI 1.43-1.81; P < 0.0001). The direction of association was generally consistent across exploratory subgroups defined by treatment category, age, geographic region, and NLR cut-off. Leave-one-out analyses did not identify a single study that changed the direction of either pooled association. Between-study heterogeneity and evidence of small-study effects warrant cautious interpretation. Elevated pretreatment NLR was associated with poorer survival outcomes in chemotherapy-treated CRC. NLR may be a readily available prognostic biomarker, but heterogeneous populations, variable outcome definitions and cut-off values, inconsistent covariate adjustment, and possible small-study effects currently limit its use for clinical decision-making. Prospective validation and methodological standardization are required before routine application. https://www.crd.york.ac.uk/PROSPERO/, identifier CRD420251136904.

papers.abstract: Mismatch repair (MMR) deficiency is uncommon in gastroenteropancreatic neuroendocrine tumours (GEP-NETs), yet it represents a critical biomarker for immune checkpoint inhibitor (ICI) eligibility. Treatment-associated reduction or loss of MMR protein expression, often without corresponding MSI-H, has been reported in colorectal adenocarcinoma, but comparable changes have not been described in neuroendocrine tumours. Persistent discordance between immunohistochemistry (IHC)-based MMR protein assessment and next-generation sequencing (NGS)-based microsatellite instability (MSI) testing is an emerging and clinically challenging phenomenon. We report a 55-year-old woman initially diagnosed with rectal NET Grade 1 on endoscopic biopsy; the tumour was upgraded to NET Grade 2 (Ki-67 approximately 20%) on the surgical resectionk specimen. Hepatic metastases were confirmed four months after resection. The first liver biopsy (January 16, 2026) demonstrated partial MMR protein loss by IHC (MLH1-, MSH2+, MSH6-, PMS2-), while concurrent NGS showed microsatellite stability (MSS) and a tumour mutational burden (TMB) of <1 mut/Mb. The patient received two cycles of surufatinib 250 mg orally once daily combined with intravenous carboplatin (500 mg, day 1) and etoposide (160 mg, days 1-3). Restaging CT demonstrated disease progression. A repeat liver biopsy (March 17, 2026) revealed complete loss of all four MMR proteins by IHC (MLH1-, MSH2-, MSH6-, PMS2-), while NGS again confirmed MSS and TMB <1 mut/Mb. To the best of our knowledge, this is the first reported case of apparent progressive complete MMR protein loss in the context of sequential platinum-based chemotherapy in metastatic rectal NET Grade 2, with persistent IHC-NGS discordance throughout. These findings raise an important question regarding how IHC-defined dMMR should be interpreted in the absence of NGS-confirmed MSI-H, and highlight the complexity of immunotherapy eligibility decisions in rare tumour types. Prospective data are needed to guide clinical practice.

papers.abstract: Ginsenoside Rb2 has demonstrated antitumor activity in multiple malignancies, yet its role in cervical cancer and the underlying mechanism remain unclear. This study investigated the effects of Rb2 on cervical cancer progression and explored whether metabolic reprogramming contributes to PD-L1 regulation. Cell proliferation, migration, invasion, glycolytic activity, lactate production, histone lactylation, and PD-L1 expression were evaluated in cervical cancer cells using CCK-8, EdU, colony formation, wound-healing, Transwell, Seahorse analysis, RT-qPCR, western blotting, flow cytometry, and ChIP-qPCR. LDHA regulation was examined by protein and mRNA stability assays, pharmacological inhibition, lysosome immunoprecipitation, gain- and loss-of-function studies, co-immunoprecipitation, molecular docking, and biotinylated Rb2 pull-down assays. T-cell function was assessed by Jurkat T-cell-tumor cell co-culture and IL-2 ELISA. Xenograft models and clinical samples were used for validation. Rb2 significantly inhibited cervical cancer cell proliferation, migration, invasion, and xenograft tumor growth, reducing HeLa and SiHa cell viability by approximately 23.4% and 25.7%, respectively. Rb2 selectively downregulated PD-L1 and suppressed glycolysis and lactate production, with reduced H3K18la/H4K12la lactylation at the PD-L1 promoter. LDHA was the primary glycolytic enzyme reduced by Rb2, without changes in its mRNA. Rb2 decreased LDHA protein stability and promoted its autophagy-lysosome-dependent degradation, with p62 required and the p62-LDHA interaction enhanced by Rb2. Rb2-pretreated tumor cells restored IL-2 production by co-cultured Jurkat T cells, whereas LDHA overexpression reversed this effect. LDHA overexpression partially rescued Rb2's effects, and LDHA correlated positively with PD-L1 in cervical cancer tissues. Rb2 suppresses cervical cancer progression by promoting p62-dependent autophagic degradation of LDHA, thereby inhibiting glycolysis-associated H3K18la and PD-L1 transcription. These findings reveal a p62/LDHA/H3K18la/PD-L1 signaling axis through which Rb2 exerts its antitumor effects.

papers.abstract: Midbody remnants (MBRs), once considered inert cytokinetic debris, are now recognized as architecturally specialized, translationally active organelles whose functions reflect the mode of cell division. This review compares MBR biology in symmetric somatic mitosis and asymmetric oocyte meiosis. In somatic cells, MBRs can be retained or secreted as large extracellular vesicles that carry midbody proteins, RNAs, and translation machinery; their enrichment in stem and cancer cells implicates them in cell-state regulation and identifies them as promising, though unvalidated, substrates for liquid-biopsy biomarkers and therapeutic targeting. In oocytes, meiotic midbodies form a distinctive ring-cap architecture that concentrates local translation and restricts maternal products to the egg, thereby supporting developmental competence. Together, these studies establish division mode as a key determinant of midbody architecture, cargo, fate, and translational potential, linking cytokinesis to cancer biology and reproductive medicine.

papers.abstract: Attention deficit-hyperactivity disorder (ADHD) is a medical condition that is present in approximately 2.5% of adults worldwide and manifests in a variety of different ways across the lifespan. Adults with ADHD often have coexisting psychiatric disorders such as anxiety, mood, sleep, substance use, and personality disorders and are at increased risk for coexisting somatic conditions such as obesity, cardiovascular and cerebrovascular disease, type 1 and type 2 diabetes, and immune and inflammatory conditions. Hence, such adults may be seen by clinicians providing care for a wide range of psychiatric and somatic conditions. Nevertheless, ADHD remains unrecognized and undiagnosed in many persons. Assessment requires interviewing of the patient for core ADHD symptoms, coexisting conditions, and their functional effects, which can be facilitated by using standardized rating scales. Key components of treatment are psychoeducation and psychostimulant or nonstimulant medication, mostly in combination with psychosocial interventions and lifestyle guidance.

papers.abstract: Recent evidence implicates a metabolic switch in afferent spinal circuits as a key driver of the transition from acute pain– to chronic pain–related behaviors in mice after tissue injury, yet the cellular substrates and functional consequences remain incompletely defined. Using a combination of pharmacological and genetic approaches, we investigated whether metabolic reprogramming in spinal cord cell populations constitutes a causal mechanism linking peripheral injury to the progression to pain chronicity. After peripheral injury induced by a hindpaw formalin injection in mice, single-nucleus RNA sequencing (snRNA-seq) revealed that spinal oligodendrocytes down-regulated transcripts for myelin protein synthesis and up-regulated transcripts important for lipid biosynthesis. Comparative lipidomics showed that this resource reallocation after peripheral injury was associated with disrupted spinal myelin composition. Moreover, axonal integrity was compromised, causing neuronal accumulation of amyloid precursor protein, enhanced β-site amyloid precursor protein–cleaving enzyme 1 (BACE1) expression, and increased insoluble amyloid-β 42 (Aβ 42 ) during a critical temporal window for the transition to pain chronicity. Blocking Aβ 42 production by BACE1 inhibition or clearing Aβ 42 by intrathecal 4G8 monoclonal antibody injection prevented the emergence of persistent pain after hindpaw formalin injection. Oligodendrocyte-specific deletion of N -acylethanolamine acid amidase, a key regulator of cell metabolism and pain, prevented Aβ 42 release and chronic pain development induced by formalin injection or sciatic nerve ligation. These findings uncover an unexpected mechanistic link between chronic pain and amyloid pathology and identify the NAAA→Aβ 42 pathway as a target for disease-modifying intervention.

papers.abstract: Abstract Background Primary mitochondrial diseases affect 1 in 4300 livebirths and cause early death or lifelong disability but our understanding of their impact on survival and causes of death is limited. There is conflicting evidence about whether they cause an increased incidence of cancer. We aimed to determine survival, causes of death and risk of developing cancer in people with mitochondrial disease by linking genetic results with routinely collected healthcare data at a national scale. Methods Individuals with mitochondrial diseases were identified in England (population 60.2 million) by National Health Service diagnostic laboratories and Genomics England. A curated cohort was assembled. Individual consent was not required because the National Disease Registration Service has legal permission to collect patient data. We used national datasets to find out the vital status, cause of death and any cancer diagnoses for each individual. Kaplan-Meier survival, Cox regression model and standardised cancer incidence ratio were analysed. Results 1266 unique individuals were identified, with 1164 having a known region in England. Following clinical review, 1107 were included (527 males, 580 females, median age 48 years, age range from infancy to 90 years). 74% had a mitochondrial DNA diagnosis and 26% had nuclear genetic diagnosis. 170 were deceased. 159 were diagnosed during childhood (14.3%). Most childhood deaths were due to the underlying mitochondrial disorder. Common causes of death in adults included cardiac, cancers, and pneumonia. Survival after diagnosis varied by genetic diagnosis and by age at diagnosis with poorer survival for people diagnosed during childhood (hazard ratio 2.11, p < 0.001) or older age (2.83, p < 0.001) and those with recessive POLG disease (hazard ratio 3.06, p < 0.001). For the whole cohort, survival at 10 years after genetic diagnosis was 80.3% (95% confidence interval 76.9% to 83.7%) and survival at 20 years after diagnosis was 58.9% (95% confidence interval 49.6% to 70.0%). Standardised cancer incidence ratios did not show a difference in cancer incidence compared to the general population. Conclusions Survival was much longer than anticipated, with differences due to the precise genetic diagnosis and age at onset. Despite prior contradictory evidence, there was no increased cancer risk in this large cohort.
